candidates.name: Land Double-Certificate, Overlap & Title-Risk Detection
candidates.hypothesis:
Land registration is a state monopoly under ATR/BPN (PP 24/1997, amended
PP 18/2021). A citizen or PPAT checks a certificate's status via Sentuh
Tanahku (free app, Digital-KTP-integrated 2026) or BHUMI map portal, or a
PPAT runs an "electronic certificate check" at BPN before an AJB.
Mortgages register electronically via HT-el since 2020. But 89.4 million
of 97.4 million certificated parcels (92.2%) remain paper as of March
2026, and pre-1997 certificates sit outside the digital cadastral map,
particularly KW4-6 "unmapped" parcels — exactly where boundary conflicts
and duplicate issuance occur (research/industries/land-registry.md,
ATR/BPN via Infonasional 2026; Kompas Properti, May-June 2026). Nobody
outside BPN can independently reconstruct issuance history; BPN's own
process is the source of documented double-issuance.
candidates.workflow:
State: Sentuh Tanahku (free, self-check, Digital-KTP-integrated 2026),
BHUMI portal, e-certificate program (Permen ATR 3/2023, only 7.8% of
stock converted by March 2026), HT-el electronic mortgage registration,
PTSL mass titling (~1.87M parcels targeted 2026 after budget cuts),
Satgas Anti-Mafia Tanah (enforcement, post-hoc, not a DD product).
Minister has stated a 2028 blockchain/smart-contract target — a plan, not
a deployment. No title insurance exists in Indonesia: legal scholarship
explicitly identifies this as an unfilled gap ("lembaga asuransi
pendaftaran tanah... belum" — Jurnal Bina Mulia Hukum). No dedicated
Indonesian title-verification/DD startup was found (Rukamen and similar
sites are informational blogs); DD is handled manually by law firms
(Fast Legal Indonesia, Putranto Alliance) on a bespoke basis. Global
comparable: the US title-insurance industry (First American, Stewart,
Fidelity National) is a mature multi-billion-dollar market built on
exactly this uncertainty — structurally absent in Indonesia.
candidates.buyer:
Named buyers: bank risk/legal departments doing KPR and commercial
collateral DD (currently pay KJPP appraisers Rp1-3.5M/property for
*value* appraisal, not title-risk verification — 99.co, brighton.co.id);
PPAT/notaries, who face civil liability under KUHPerdata Art. 1365
(onrechtmatige daad) and Art. 1243 (contractual negligence) for missed
double certificates (media.neliti.com); property buyers and law firms
doing manual DD on larger transactions. No cross-border party.
candidates.trustFailure:
- Mbah Tupon (Bantul, 2025): a 68-year-old illiterate farmer's 1,655 m²
  certificate was transferred to another name and pledged for a Rp1.5
  billion bank loan without his knowledge; 7 perpetrators, incl. a former
  village head/DPRD member, arrested April 2025, convicted November 2025;
  certificate returned April 2026 (Detik, 2025; Antara Yogyakarta, 2026).
- Malang double certificates: BPN Kabupaten Malang issued a 2024 SHM over
  land already covered by a 1994 SHM held by residents 30 years; dozens
  filed reports with Polda Jatim (Beritajatim, 2025).
- Case load: 3,260 land dispute/conflict/crime cases recorded through
  September 2025 (Detik Finance, 24 Nov 2025).
- Satgas Anti-Mafia Tanah 2025: 90 cases resolved (target 65), 185
  suspects named, 14,315 ha saved, Rp23.265-23.38 trillion averted
  (figure varies by outlet, same ATR/BPN release) (Harianjogja, BorneoTribun,
  Antara Sumbar, Asajabar — December 2025).
- Double/forged certificates persist into the e-certificate era (Tatkala,
  June 2026).
candidates.killTest:
- **K1 Data access — PASSES, narrower scope.** Sentuh Tanahku/BHUMI
  per-parcel lookup is free/public; court/PTUN filings are public; a
  paying customer (bank, notary) can legally query these and contribute
  its own case history to a compounding flagged-parcel database — a
  private title-abstractor model, not requiring BPN cooperation. A fuller
  version predicting BPN's own future insider-mediated issuance errors is
  NOT achievable without bulk historical access BPN doesn't grant.
- **K2 Oracle bound — PASSES for detection, not adjudication.** Overlap
  between two already-issued certificates is inferable by geo-matching
  boundaries across the digitized cadastral layer plus court filings.
  Determining who is legally correct in a pre-1997 girik/letter-C chain
  dispute is closer to a fabricated-at-source, off-system-collusion
  problem (village-level, insider-mediated per land-registry.md) and out
  of scope for a detection/flagging product.
- **K3 Absorption — PASSES (no 12-month evidence found).** ATR/BPN's
  digitization (e-certificates, PTSL, Sentuh Tanahku) improves the
  state's own registry but is not a bank/buyer-facing DD product; Satgas
  Anti-Mafia Tanah is enforcement, not prevention. No cited roadmap for
  any state actor to ship a third-party diligence product in 12 months.
- **K4 Bootstrap bar — PASSES, moderate evidence.** Named segment
  (notaries, regional banks, law firms), real Indonesian ACV comparable
  (KJPP fee), subscription model avoiding enterprise-sales dependency;
  reachable-count figure is inferred.
candidates.scores:
- Severity 9 — Rp23.3T+ averted in 2025 alone, Rp1.5B+ individual
  exposure, criminal convictions, 3,260 active dispute cases.
- Revenue quality 5 — plausible segment with a real adjacent ACV
  comparable, but reachable-count evidence is inferred.
- WTP 5 — legal liability creates real latent incentive, but no evidence
  anyone pays for third-party verification beyond the free state check.
- Data position 4 — underlying registry data is free/commodity (Sentuh
  Tanahku open to any citizen); accumulating flagged-case layer is a
  secondary, unproven asset.
- Absorption distance 6 — BPN's digitization is adjacent but doesn't
  cover third-party DD-as-a-service; no cited roadmap into this function.
- Competition 7 — no productized Indonesian competitor found; only
  manual, bespoke law-firm DD and a documented absence of title insurance.
- Moat 7 — a cross-customer flagged-parcel database compounds: a parcel
  flagged risky by one bank benefits every subsequent customer checking
  it.

Weighted = 0.20(9)+0.20(5)+0.15(5)+0.15(4)+0.10(6)+0.10(7)+0.10(7) = **6.2**
candidates.whatWouldKill:
Evidence that ATR/BPN opens bulk historical-parcel API access to licensed
third parties (commoditizing the data layer), or that a bank
consortium/OJK mandates a shared collateral title-risk registry with
state backing on a funded timeline.

sources.raw: research/industries/land-registry.md (Program A prior, same primary sources)

candidates.killReason: **REFUTED.** ATR/BPN Sentuh Tanahku "Berbagi Akses" (24 Jun 2026) gives buyers a free consent-based pre-purchase check; incumbent price is Rp50k via PPAT; residual duplicates are 92.2% paper and not record-inferable.

candidates.name: Fidusia Collateral Reconciliation & Duplicate-Pledge Detection
candidates.hypothesis: A fidusia guarantee (jaminan fidusia) lets a debtor keep possession of collateral (a vehicle, inventory, receivables) while legal title sits with the creditor until the loan is repaid. Truth about "is this asset already pledged elsewhere" is established today through three disconnected systems: (1) **Ditjen AHU's Fidusia Online registry** (fidusia.ahu.go.id) — the legal system of record, searchable by financing-company name and agreement number, not by chassis/plate number; (2) **SLIK** (OJK's credit information system) — debtor credit history, not a collateral-object registry; (3) **Rapindo**, a private asset-registration platform owned outright by APPI (the financing-company association), operating under a regulatory mandate (POJK 47/2020) requiring financing companies to register objects at an asset-recording institution. Rapindo records chassis/frame/serial numbers specifically to catch double-financing and double-pledging among member institutions, reporting 32.875 million assets on file by June 30, 2024 (Bisnis.com, Aug 13, 2024). Reconciliation of AHU's own registration data against OJK's supervisory financing data is a separate, government-internal process a July 2025 audit found badly broken.
candidates.buyer: Two distinct buyer segments exist. (1) Institutional: multifinance companies and banks originating vehicle/asset-backed loans, who already pay AHU's PNBP registration fee (tiered Rp50,000–Rp13,300,000 by collateral value, PP 28/2019) and, if APPI members, Rapindo's membership/query fees. (2) Government: Ditjen AHU (Kemenkum) and OJK, who bear the reconciliation cost of keeping the legal registry internally consistent — this is a state budget line, not a private one.
candidates.trustFailure:
- BPK audit (2022–2024 period): discrepancy of up to 35 million transactions between OJK financing reports and Ditjen AHU fidusia registration data; causes cited include no separation between new registrations and amendment records, and double fidusia guarantees on the same object; estimated state revenue loss >Rp20 billion (kepri.kemenkum.go.id, "Perkuat Akurasi Data Nasional…," undated 2025 government release summarizing the BPK finding — primary BPK LHP not independently retrieved this pass, so treat as government-secondary, not primary).
- Fidusia PNBP contributed 65–85% of Ditjen AHU's non-tax state revenue over the last five years (same source) — showing the registry's fiscal centrality.
- Samuel Hartono Goenawan case, Surabaya District Court (proceedings dated July 29, 2021 — differs from the brief's "2022" hint): a Mitsubishi Pajero Sport's BPKB, held in fidusia by U Finance, was secretly re-pledged to a private lender for Rp315 million, part of debt reaching Rp1 billion across three vehicles (surabayapagi.com).
- OJK and Ditjen AHU signed a formal data-exchange cooperation agreement July 16, 2025 explicitly to strengthen fidusia oversight (CNBC Indonesia, Jul 24, 2025) — itself an admission the gap is live.
candidates.killTest:
- **K1 (Data access): PASS.** Institutional buyers already hold or can obtain access to AHU's public registry, their own SLIK credentials, and Rapindo membership.
- **K2 (Oracle bound): PASS.** Duplicate-pledge truth is inferable from existing digital records (AHU, SLIK, Rapindo) for the institutional segment; informal/off-registry lending (e.g., the Agus Wijaya case) is genuinely off-oracle and excluded.
- **K3 (Absorption): FAIL — KILL.** Rapindo is a regulator-mandated (POJK 47/2020), industry-owned incumbent already performing double-pledge/double-financing detection for the institutional segment (32.875M assets, live since 2019; Bisnis.com Aug 2024), and OJK–Ditjen AHU signed a direct data-reconciliation cooperation agreement Jul 16, 2025 (CNBC Indonesia) addressing the government-side gap. Both the private and public absorption paths are already funded and operating.
- **K4 (Bootstrap bar): FAIL.** With the institutional segment's exact function already served by a mandated near-free incumbent, and no evidenced ACV for a consumer wedge, no credible >=$1M ARR path survives without either replicating Rapindo's regulatory mandate or building an enterprise marketplace-partnership motion.
candidates.scores:
- Severity: 7 — BPK-documented multi-year national-scale discrepancy with fiscal impact >Rp20B and dedicated agency response.
- Bootstrap revenue quality: 3 — institutional ACV undercut by mandated incumbent; consumer ACV has no Indonesian comparable.
- WTP: 4 — budget exists but is already captured by Rapindo/AHU/SLIK spend.
- Data position: 4 — evidence (AHU public search, SLIK) is a commodity feed, not exclusive.
- Absorption distance: 3 — incumbent (Rapindo) already occupies the exact function.
- Competition: 3 — funded, regulator-mandated incumbent with clear Indonesian traction.
- Moat: 3 — no cross-customer network effect available once Rapindo owns the network.

**Weighted: 4.1**
candidates.whatWouldKill: Already killed: Rapindo (APPI/POJK 47/2020) plus the July 2025 OJK–AHU reconciliation PKS jointly demonstrate the exact function is funded, mandated, and operating for the addressable institutional buyer.

sources.raw: kepri.kemenkum.go.id (BPK finding summary, 2025); CNBC Indonesia, Jul 24, 2025; Bisnis.com, Aug 13, 2024; CNN Indonesia, Aug 20, 2019; rapindo.co.id; surabayapagi.com (case dated Jul 29, 2021); PP 28/2019 PNBP tariff via harga.web.id; idscore.id.

candidates.killReason: Rapindo (APPI, POJK 47/2020-mandated) already runs double-pledge detection over 32.875M assets; OJK–AHU reconciliation PKS signed 16 Jul 2025.

candidates.name: EUDR Plot-Level Origin Evidence (Coffee/Cocoa/Palm/Timber)
candidates.hypothesis: EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) due-diligence statements require exporters to submit high-precision plot-level geolocation proving each shipment is deforestation-free (post-Dec 31, 2020 cutoff) and legally produced. In Indonesia, that evidence chain is thin: 98% of coffee area is smallholder plantings averaging 1–2 ha (USDA FAS Coffee Annual, Jakarta, Report ID2025-0021, May 19, 2025); over 60% of palm smallholders lack land certificates (infosawit.com/sawitindonesia.com, 2025); and Koltiva states only ~12% of downstream firms have any traceability system in place (Koltiva/marketersmedia, Jul 24, 2025). Geolocation "evidence" is typically produced one of three ways: (1) exporter-commissioned polygon-mapping contractors (Koltiva and peers) who *collect* coordinates from farmers, often for a fee; (2) government e-STDB (farmer registration), proceeding district-by-district and slowly (Pesawaran district: 1,120 farmers/1,382 ha — kabarsdgs.com, 2026); (3) desk estimation from administrative boundaries where no field survey occurred. None of these routes independently *verifies* a submitted polygon is genuine, unique to one farmer, and not reused across declarations or borrowed from an adjacent permit — collection and verification are conflated today.
candidates.buyer: EU-facing exporters and traders of coffee, cocoa, palm, and timber who must file a Due Diligence Statement (DDS) per shipment and bear legal/financial exposure (market exclusion, EU customs holds) if a submission is later found fraudulent or non-compliant. This is the buyer for a verification-only wedge; the farmer/smallholder is not the buyer (extension/mapping-cost subsidy is typically paid by the exporter or a program, not the smallholder).
candidates.trustFailure:
- Only ~1% of 6.2 million ha of Indonesian smallholder palm land is ISPO-certified despite the scheme running over a decade (majalahhortus.com, 2025) — a proxy for low verified-plot documentation; close to, but not confirmed identical to, the brief's specific "1.07% e-STDB, July 2024" figure (**unverified as stated**).
- INDEF survey: 94% of farmers surveyed across three provinces were unaware of EUDR rules (mediaindonesia.com; survey year not confirmed in the retrieved excerpt).
- Koltiva: "only 12% of downstream firms have traceability systems in place," urging "inclusive segregation to prevent smallholder exclusion" (marketersmedia, Jul 24, 2025).
- The regulation's compliance runway moved twice — Dec 2024 → Dec 2025 → Dec 2026 for medium/large operators, Jun 2027 micro/small (Reg. (EU) 2025/2650, per H2 Compliance/PSQR, Dec 2025) — the repeated delay itself signals how far verified-data readiness lags the legal requirement.
- USDA FAS confirms EU (via Belgium/Germany) is a top-2 destination for Indonesian coffee, over 1.4 million bags Mar 2024–Feb 2025 (USDA FAS Coffee Annual ID2025-0021, May 2025). The brief's claim that USDA FAS documented "desk-drawn" coffee polygons could not be confirmed in the pages retrieved (**unverified as stated**).
candidates.killTest:
- **K1 (Data access): PASS.** For a verification-only wedge, the exporter (paying customer) controls its own DDS submissions and can license third-party satellite/deforestation datasets independently of farmer cooperation.
- **K2 (Oracle bound): PASS.** Deforestation-cutoff satellite imagery, polygon-uniqueness cross-referencing, and boundary-plausibility checks are inferable from existing signals — the same class of evidence EU's own reference system and Global Forest Watch already use.
- **K3 (Absorption): FAIL — KILL.** Koltiva already owns the customer relationship for 19,000+ upstream/downstream businesses and already ships a named "Data Verification" product line (koltiva.com; agreads.com, Feb 2026) — the exact function proposed. The National Dashboard Indonesia (funded, EU co-financed, operator appointed, launched 2025) reinforces this on the government side, explicitly claiming the "accurate, reliable, immutable" verification mandate.
- **K4 (Bootstrap bar): FAIL.** With the addressable exporter base's compliance relationship and budget substantially already held by Koltiva, no independent bottom-up path to $1M ARR survives without displacing that incumbency.
candidates.scores:
- Severity: 7 — documented, multi-source readiness gap (certification rates, awareness survey, traceability-system coverage) with real market-access consequences and a moving compliance deadline.
- Bootstrap revenue quality: 3 — customer base largely already captured by Koltiva; no clean Indonesian ACV comparable for a standalone verification product.
- WTP: 5 — real compliance budget exists but is largely already committed to incumbents.
- Data position: 4 — verification relies on largely public/purchasable satellite datasets, a commodity feed available to any competitor including Koltiva.
- Absorption distance: 3 — adjacent incumbent (Koltiva) already ships the named function; government dashboard reinforces.
- Competition: 3 — funded incumbent (Koltiva) with deep Indonesian/regional traction, plus multiple funded foreign entrants.
- Moat: 4 — mostly per-customer integration lock-in; Koltiva's incumbency blocks new cross-customer network effects.

**Weighted: 4.4**
candidates.whatWouldKill: Already killed: Koltiva's existing "Data Verification" product line serving 19,000+ businesses, plus the EU-co-funded National Dashboard Indonesia explicitly targeting "accurate, reliable, immutable" geolocation across the same commodities.

sources.raw: USDA FAS Coffee Annual, Jakarta, ID2025-0021, May 19, 2025; infosawit.com/sawitindonesia.com, 2025; majalahhortus.com, 2025; mediaindonesia.com (INDEF survey); marketersmedia/Koltiva, Jul 24, 2025; koltiva.com; agreads.com, Feb 2026; rm.id; Mongabay, Apr 2025; betahita.id/theiconomics.com; H2 Compliance/PSQR, Dec 2025; satelligence.com; orbify.com; meridia.land; efi.int; kabarsdgs.com, 2026.

candidates.killReason: Koltiva ships a named "Data Verification" EUDR product (Feb 2026) across 19,000+ business relationships; National Dashboard Indonesia reinforces via state channel.

candidates.name: Government Program Roster Identity Resolution (DTKS/e-RDKK/Dapodik/Payroll)
candidates.hypothesis: Four government program rosters — DTKS (social-assistance targeting, Kemensos), e-RDKK (fertilizer-subsidy eligibility, Kementan), Dapodik (student data underlying BOS funding, Kemendikbudristek), and ASN/PNS payroll (BKN/BKD) — carry duplicate, deceased, or fictitious NIKs because each is compiled on its own cadence rather than continuously reconciled against Dukcapil's population/death registry and against each other. Today's process is periodic and manual: village musyawarah for DTKS proposals, door-to-door BPS census sweeps (Regsosek), self-reported ASN re-verification (MySAPK), ad hoc ministry "pemutakhiran" drives — not event-driven reconciliation.
candidates.buyer: Named potential buyers: BPKP and BPK (state audit bodies with a standing audit mandate), Kemensos/BPS (already building their own fix — see K3), Kementan/pemda agriculture offices for e-RDKK, Kemendikbudristek/Disdikbud for Dapodik/BOS, and BKN/BKD for payroll. Cross-organizational: Dukcapil holds the ground-truth population/death registry and gates access via renewable two-year data-cooperation agreements — a private vendor needs Dukcapil's cooperation for NIK-matching rights (dukcapil.kemendagri.go.id).
candidates.trustFailure:
- BPK: 10,992,479 household members with invalid NIK, 16,373,682 with invalid KK numbers, 86,465 duplicate NIKs in DTKS data as of Jan 2020 (CNN Indonesia, 2022, reporting FY2021 audit) — dated but still the most-cited baseline.
- BPK: Rp6.93 trillion in misallocated PKH/BPNT/BST assistance, incl. payments to deceased recipients still listed as KPM and to households never in DTKS (CNN Indonesia, Suara.com, Sindonews, all reporting the same FY2021 audit, 2022). No more recent equivalent BPK figure found; historical baseline, not a fresh 2025–26 finding.
- Ombudsman RI: 13% of ~6.3M e-RDKK-registered farmer NIKs invalid, 68%+ of "valid" farmers did not redeem subsidized fertilizer 2022–2024 (ombudsman.go.id, 2025).
- BKN "97,000 ghost PNS": a 2014-vintage finding, resurfaced 2021; BKN itself says resolved by 2016 via MySAPK (CNN Indonesia, idxchannel, viva.co.id). **Stale** — no 2025–26 equivalent found; weak sub-case.
- Dapodik: ~11,000 alleged phantom SMK students in Banten, ~Rp17 billion alleged loss, reported July 2026 by a citizen monitoring group (DPP-FPK) — recent but single-source, still "diduga" (alleged) (mediakriminalitas.com, July 2026).
candidates.killTest:
- **K1 Data access — PASS.** Government auditors (BPKP/BPK) have a legal mandate to the underlying data; a private-vendor route also exists — Dukcapil already runs formal two-year cooperation agreements with ~242 institutions, ~200 more (BPRs, insurers, fintechs) in queue (dukcapil.kemendagri.go.id) — cooperation is realistically obtainable, if slow.
- **K2 Oracle bound — PASS.** Duplicate/deceased/fictitious NIK status is a well-defined, recorded fact resolvable by cross-referencing Dukcapil's civil registry — a database-matching problem, not off-system collusion or a physically-fabricated truth.
- **K3 Absorption — FAIL (kill).** DTSEN v3, announced ready 8 July 2026, has Dukcapil performing continuous identity matching as a core, funded function that explicitly replaces DTKS — the single largest and best-evidenced sub-case here (Rp6.93T, 10.99M invalid NIKs). This is a named, dated, funded government implementation already entering the exact function proposed for the flagship sub-case (itera.ac.id, 2026). e-RDKK, Dapodik, and payroll show weaker or no comparable absorption, but the candidate as scoped includes DTKS, and its flagship piece is being absorbed.
- **K4 Bootstrap bar — FAIL.** The remaining non-absorbed sub-cases (e-RDKK, Dapodik, payroll) route through LPSE government-tender procurement to a small number of ministry/pemda buyers — no self-serve/API channel or Indonesian pricing comparable found; also fails the founder gate (G6).

**Survives: no — killed on K3 (DTSEN v3 is a funded, dated, named government absorption of the flagship DTKS sub-case) and independently on K4 (remaining sub-cases require government-tender enterprise sales, no self-serve path evidenced).**
candidates.scores:
- Severity 7 — large, recurring, institutionally-tracked losses across registries (Rp6.93T bansos, Rp17B alleged Dapodik) with standing BPK/Ombudsman/BPKP oversight, though the largest figure is 2021-vintage and the newest (2026) is single-source/alleged.
- Bootstrap revenue 3 — no self-serve channel or Indonesian ACV comparable found; buyer is government-tender-gated.
- WTP 5 — audit/oversight budgets exist at BPKP/BPK/pemda level but are slow-moving, tender-gated, not owned by any single accessible buyer.
- Data position 3 — the Dukcapil feed, once an MOU is obtained, is the same commodity feed available to any cooperating institution — no accumulation edge for a private vendor.
- Absorption distance 3 — a concrete absorber (DTSEN) already exists with cited 12-month evidence for the flagship sub-case.
- Competition 5 — no dedicated private startup found for this niche, but the state's own DTSEN/Dapodik-filter systems occupy the space.
- Moat 3 — any private-vendor relationship is single-tenant/switchable per ministry, since Dukcapil gates data equally to all.
- **Weighted: 4.3**
candidates.whatWouldKill: Already killed as scoped. Worth revisiting only if DTSEN v3's rollout stalls or fails to functionally cover identity resolution (contradicting itera.ac.id), or if a specific non-government buyer (e.g., an NGO/media consortium with budget) is identified for the e-RDKK/Dapodik-only wedge.

sources.raw: CNN Indonesia, Suara.com, Sindonews, tvOne (BPK DTKS/bansos findings, 2022 reporting FY2021 audit); ombudsman.go.id (e-RDKK findings, 2025); idxchannel.com, idntimes.com, indozone.id, viva.co.id (97k PNS case, 2014/2021); mediakriminalitas.com (Banten Dapodik case, July 2026); pusatinformasi.rumahpendidikan.kemendikdasmen.go.id (NIK Tidak Padan filter); itera.ac.id (DTSEN v3, July 2026); dukcapil.kemendagri.go.id (data-access cooperation framework); askopindo.co.id, pdiperjuanganbali.id, kyowa-indonesia.co.id (DTSEN/DTSEN desil system, 2026); privy.id, vida.id (identity-verification vendor scope).

candidates.killReason: DTSEN v3 (ready 8 Jul 2026) has Dukcapil continuous identity-matching built in as a funded function, absorbing the flagship DTKS slice.

candidates.name: Pit-to-Shipment Ore Provenance & ESG Evidence
candidates.hypothesis: To sell nickel ore, an IUP (mining license) holder needs an ESDM-approved RKAB, a paid PNBP royalty, a surveyor grade/tonnage certificate (Sucofindo, Surveyor Indonesia), and — since early 2025 — a SIMBARA transaction record linking ESDM, the Finance Ministry, and customs. SIMBARA verifies a shipment has valid paperwork and paid royalties; it does not verify the ore physically originated inside the licensed pit. That gap is exploited by "dokumen terbang" (flying documents): legitimate RKAB paperwork rented out to launder ore mined outside license boundaries, trading at a 10-12.5% discount because everyone knows it is unverifiable (Bloomberg Technoz, 19 May 2026). Downstream, EU battery-regulation due diligence is satisfied today by scheme audits — RMAP+ (Harita Nickel, per a Jul 2026 Finance Ministry op-ed) and IRMA (PT Vale, stage-two audit, Dec 2025) — paper/process audits, not satellite-verified pit-boundary evidence.
candidates.workflow: Government: SIMBARA (fiscal/customs gatekeeping, 5 commodities by 2026; a Jul 2026 Finance Ministry op-ed frames it toward a "digital chain of custody" aligned with battery-passport concepts, admitting RKAB/interoperability gaps); Danantara's proposed one-door export regime (miners worried about SIMBARA overlap, Jul 2026); AI export surveillance layered onto SIMBARA (Luhut, May 2026). Global vendors: Circulor, RCS Global/SLR, Minespider — OEM/battery end, no verified upstream Indonesian pit-level integration. Baliola (Mandala Chain) pitches blockchain traceability, no verified mining deployment or funding through mid-2026. Audit schemes RMAP+ (Harita) and IRMA (Vale, stage-two) are the path EU notified bodies actually accept.
candidates.buyer: Cross-organizational: the party bearing compliance risk is not the party controlling the mine. Named segments: OEM/battery-maker sustainability teams sourcing Indonesian nickel; RMAP/IRMA-scheme auditors needing corroboration beyond site-visit interviews; EU notified bodies verifying due-diligence reports. Legitimate miners proving they are not "dokumen terbang" ore are a secondary, smaller-budget segment. The corrupt document-issuers and miners benefiting from ambiguity have no incentive to pay.
candidates.economics: No Indonesian or comparable global ACV was found for a satellite-x-license-polygon ESG-evidence service sold to auditors/OEMs (search, 2026-07; unverified). The reachable buyer universe is thin: RMAP/IRMA-accredited auditors number in the dozens globally, and OEMs with disclosed Indonesian nickel exposure are a short, named list (Harita, Vale's customers). Reaching $1M ARR from a few dozen accounts needs a high per-account ACV (illustratively $20,000-100,000/yr) with no cited Indonesian precedent, and buyer acquisition looks consultative/relationship-driven, not self-serve (tension with G6). New evidence weakens urgency: the EU Council adopted a "stop-the-clock" law on 18 Jul 2025 pausing battery-regulation due-diligence timelines, removing the forcing deadline that would pressure OEMs to buy now. Evidence quality: **weak** — segment named but small, ACV unverified, and the regulatory clock prior research cited as urgency driver has since been paused.
candidates.trustFailure:
- **Antam Mandiodo block**: illegal ore sales in Southeast Sulawesi using fraudulent RKAB documents; state loss Rp5.7 trillion (Kejaksaan Agung, 2023); eight defendants sentenced April 2024, including former Minerba Director-General Ridwan Djamaludin. Collusion-tainted — officials issued/laundered the very documents the state system relies on, why paper-trail-only verification cannot be trusted for this fraud class.
- **Illegal exports**: KPK found 5.3 Mt of nickel ore shipped to China 2020-June 2022 despite an export ban, worth ~US$963M/Rp14.5T, detected via a BPS-China customs discrepancy, not any domestic provenance system (KPK; Tempo, 2023).
- **2026 recurrence**: "dokumen terbang" reported rampant again in 2026, driven by a quota deficit (~260-270 Mt approved RKAB vs ~294 Mt smelter demand), discounting laundered ore 10-12.5% — after SIMBARA became mandatory (Bloomberg Technoz, May 2026).
- **Scale**: Bareskrim mapped 1,517 illegal mining sites across 33 provinces in 2025 (Bisnis, Dec 2025); four Maluku Utara miners fined Feb 2026, one Rp2.27 trillion for mining 234 ha outside license (Mongabay, 2026).
candidates.killTest:
- **K1 (Data access): PASS.** Satellite imagery (Planet, Maxar, Sentinel/ESA) is commercially or freely purchasable independent of any Indonesian party's cooperation; license-polygon boundaries are part of Minerba's MODI/MOMS licensing data. An auditor or OEM can commission independent boundary-compliance analysis without the audited miner or a corrupt SIMBARA administrator cooperating.
- **K2 (Oracle bound): PASS, scope-limited.** Pit-boundary encroachment and surface-disturbance signals are directly inferable from satellite time-series without off-system collusion. Ore *tonnage and grade* fraud (the core of dokumen terbang and Mandiodo) is not — it still depends on surveyor certificates, the exact paper trail corrupted in Mandiodo. The product must scope to boundary/ESG evidence, not volumetric fraud, to keep K2 clean.
- **K3 (Absorption): PASS**, for the narrow satellite-ESG-evidence function. SIMBARA's 2026 direction is fiscal/logistics chain-of-custody, not remote-sensing ESG verification; no cited 12-month roadmap targets this exact function.
- **K4 (Bootstrap bar): FAIL.** No Indonesian/comparable ACV evidence; thin, consultative-sale buyer universe; the regulatory forcing function prior research relied on (Feb 2027 battery-passport deadline) was paused by the EU's July 2025 stop-the-clock law.

**Survives: no.**
candidates.scores:
- Severity 7 — multi-trillion-rupiah documented losses (Mandiodo Rp5.7T, illegal exports Rp14.5T, single Rp2.27T fine) and jailed officials, but this severity is largely fiscal/tonnage fraud the narrow ESG-evidence product does not itself address.
- Revenue quality 3 — no Indonesian or comparable ACV; thin buyer count with no first-customer route evidenced.
- WTP 6 — named budget owners (Harita, Vale) already pay for an inferior alternative (RMAP+/IRMA audits), but the Jul 2025 stop-the-clock delay softens urgency and no cited buyer pays for satellite-augmented evidence specifically.
- Data position 4 — satellite imagery is commodity/replicable; a cross-mine historical compliance database would accrue value but is unbuilt.
- Absorption distance 5 — SIMBARA's stated direction is adjacent (chain-of-custody, battery-passport-aligned language) but not a cited satellite-ESG roadmap.
- Competition 7 — this program's prior adversarial memo found no Indonesian/SEA startup doing pit-level provenance beyond a pre-traction pitch (Baliola); global vendors sit at the OEM end.
- Moat 4 — single-engagement analytical report today; a growing cross-mine polygon-compliance dataset would accrue value if built at scale.

**Weighted: 0.20(7)+0.20(3)+0.15(6)+0.15(4)+0.10(5)+0.10(7)+0.10(4) = 5.1**
candidates.whatWouldKill: SIMBARA adding geospatial pit-boundary verification itself (no roadmap found, but the Jul 2026 op-ed's framing is a watch item). The EU permanently softening standards rather than resuming the paused clock. Confirmation RMAP/IRMA auditors consider site-visit-plus-document review sufficient with no appetite for a satellite add-on (unconfirmed).

vale.com, "PT Vale Indonesia Tbk to Undergo Stage-Two IRMA Audit" (30 Dec 2025) ; https://www.baliola.io/enhancing-transparency-in-the-mining-supply-chain-with-blockchain (2025)

candidates.killReason: EU "stop-the-clock" (18 Jul 2025) paused battery-passport due-diligence timelines; buyer universe is a few dozen auditors, consultative sale.

candidates.name: Cooperative Member-Fund Integrity Monitoring (KSP + Kopdes)
candidates.hypothesis: A Koperasi Simpan Pinjam (KSP) collects mandatory/voluntary member savings and lends to members. Governance runs through the annual members' meeting (RAT), which rubber-stamps the board's self-prepared financials. External oversight is a reporting relationship, not an audit: cooperatives file data into Kemenkop's Online Data System, and since early 2025 "ODS Mandiri" (Juknis Deputi Kelembagaan No. 1/2025) lets cooperatives update their own records directly — the system, in the words of Program A's prior research, "ingests whatever the cooperative types in." Independent public-accountant audit is mandatory only for KSP/USP with capital ≥Rp5 billion, and even then nothing reconciles the audited figures with real-time bank/cash positions between annual cycles. Under UU No. 4/2023 (P2SK), cooperatives serving non-members ("open loop") must move under OJK supervision, but as of the January 2025 handover only 21 cooperatives — holding a combined Rp339 billion in assets — had transitioned (OJK/Kemenkop joint press release, 2025); the transition is targeted to conclude sometime in 2026 but the vast majority of the sector, now swelled by 80,000 new Koperasi Desa Merah Putih (Kopdes) village cooperatives launched 21 July 2025 with ~Rp5 billion in bank-channelled funding each (KBR, 2025), remains under the same self-declared regime.
candidates.buyer: Members/depositors bear the losses but have no legal access to the cooperative's bank statements or loan ledgers — the information asymmetry is the fraud's mechanism, not an incidental gap. Cooperative boards/managers control the data but, where fraudulent, have no motive to buy a tool that exposes them. Kemenkop/dinas and (for a sliver of the sector) OJK supervise but run free, self-reported systems. Banks channeling Kopdes credit (Himbara) have loan-covenant leverage over borrowing cooperatives and are the one plausible buyer with both motive and contractual data-access rights — but that collapses to a handful of enterprise accounts, not a self-serve customer base.
candidates.trustFailure:
- KSP Indosurya: prosecution valued member losses at Rp16 trillion (Viva, 2022 — headline explicitly disputes a higher Rp106 trillion figure sometimes cited elsewhere, unverified provenance); Supreme Court cassation (No. 2113 K/Pid.Sus/2023, 16 May 2023) sentenced founder Henry Surya to 18 years plus a Rp15 billion fine, June Indria to 14 years (Tempo, 2023). Funds were routed to affiliated entities while member statements showed healthy balances.
- Eight problem cooperatives (Indosurya, Sejahtera Bersama, Intidana, Lima Garuda, Timur Pratama, two Pracico entities, Wahana Berkah Sentosa) defaulted on Rp26 trillion of member claims (Kemenkop via Antara/CNBC, 2023); only Rp3.4 trillion repaid under court-homologated plans by 2024 (Tempo, 2024) — Rp22.6 trillion still unpaid.
- Kopdes Merah Putih: a CELIOS survey of 108 village heads across 34 provinces found ~65% saw significant governance gaps, warning of "structured corruption" risk (CELIOS/The Conversation, 2025); a single local report (Sergai, North Sumatra, CNEWS, April 2026 — low reliability, one outlet) alleges a Kopdes construction budget shrank from a stated Rp1.6 billion to ~Rp800 million actually built. Kemenkop has since partnered with Aspenda (regional guarantee-company association) to mitigate Kopdes fraud risk (investortrust.id, 2026).
candidates.killTest:
- **K1 Data access — FAIL.** The paying customer is either the fraud perpetrator itself (no motive, per Indosurya's affiliated-entity diversion) or an unfunded/narrow state actor (OJK covers 21 of tens of thousands of cooperatives); members/depositors lack any legal or contractual access to bank records.
- **K2 Oracle bound — PASS (conditional).** Fund diversion is inferable from bank/transaction records in principle, but Indosurya's pattern (dressing diversions as related-party loans) means interpretation, not just access, is the harder problem — moot given K1.
- **K3 Absorption — PASS (not killed).** RUU Perkoperasian/LPS Koperasi is only a DIM submitted to DPR in June 2026, not an enacted mandate; no 12-month roadmap evidence found.
- **K4 Bootstrap bar — FAIL.** No reachable self-serve customer segment with both motive and data access; the one buyer with leverage (Himbara) requires enterprise sales.
candidates.scores:
- Severity 9 — Rp26T documented member losses, criminal convictions, sector-existential (Kemenkop 2023; Tempo 2023).
- Revenue 3 — no viable self-serve buyer identified; ACV has no comparable specific to this function.
- WTP 4 — beneficiaries can't pay; state budget exists but slow/narrow (21 institutions).
- Data 3 — the core problem is that evidence is inaccessible without the fraudster's cooperation.
- Absorption 3 — adjacent state program (LPS Koperasi bill) active but unenacted.
- Competition 6 — no dedicated assurance vendor found despite two research-phase searches.
- Moat 5 — cross-cooperative fraud-pattern aggregation plausible in theory, unproven.
- Weighted: 4.9
candidates.whatWouldKill: Already killed on K1/K4. Would need either (a) LPS Koperasi enacted with a compulsory continuous-reporting mandate creating a forced buyer, or (b) a distribution deal with Himbara making bank-covenant-driven adoption self-serve rather than enterprise-sold.
candidates.killReason: Buyer is the perpetrator (Indosurya Rp16T) or an unfunded state actor (OJK covers 21 of ~130k coops); members lack record access.

candidates.name: Fictitious Tax-Invoice (Faktur) Detection & Counterparty Screening
candidates.hypothesis:
A PKP (VAT-registered) buyer in Indonesia claims input-VAT credit against a "faktur pajak" it receives from a supplier. If that invoice is later found to be TBTS (Tidak Berdasarkan Transaksi Sebenarnya — not based on an actual transaction), the buyer loses the input-VAT credit and, under Pasal 39A KUP, faces potential criminal exposure for using a fictitious invoice, even without knowing participation (muc.co.id, "Cara Aman Menghindari Risiko Faktur Pajak Fiktif").

Truth today is established in two disconnected layers. (1) DJP's Coretax system, mandatory since 1 Jan 2025, lets a buyer scan a QR code or check its dashboard to confirm an invoice is "sah" (exists, correctly formatted, active NPWP) — but this only confirms the document is real in DJP's ledger, not that the underlying transaction occurred. A shell-company issuer can register valid-looking invoices; DJP's graph-analytics/AI risk models operate DJP-side to flag issuers for audit, not to warn buyers pre-transaction (pajak.com, "Transformasi Pajak Indonesia Lewat Teknologi AI"; SE-8/PJ/2026 risk-based supervision). (2) Buyer-side, corporate tax/finance teams or outside consultants (MUC, RSM Indonesia, SW Indonesia) manually check counterparty PKP status, incorporation documents, physical-office existence and business-profile plausibility — a slow, judgment-based checklist (Enforce A, "Ini Indikasi Awal Wajib Pajak Penerbit Faktur Pajak Fiktif").
candidates.buyer: Named buyer: corporate tax/finance departments at mid-to-large PKP companies with meaningful B2B purchase volume (manufacturing, distribution, construction — sectors most cited in TBTS enforcement news), and tax-consultancy/KAP firms (MUC, RSM, SW Indonesia) who resell counterparty due-diligence as part of compliance retainers. This is single-side: the buyer bears the loss and pays; the counterparty being screened is not a customer.
candidates.trustFailure:
- Rp170.29 billion state-loss TBTS case, suspect handed to South Jakarta prosecutors 9 Jan 2026, four issuing companies (PT TNK, PT BKG, PT BTJ, PT ANL), fraud spanning 2021–2022 (DDTC News, investor.id, pajak.go.id, Jan 2026).
- "Faktur village" syndicate, Rp180 billion state loss, cross-region ring using advance-refund schemes, arrests in Banten (Kontan, pajaknow.id, 2026).
- PT SPL case: five suspects including four active "makelar" (brokers) who sourced buyers for TBTS invoices, Rp4.37 billion incl. sanctions, dossiers completed 17 Dec 2025 (pajak.go.id).
- Kaltara PT SEE TBTS case, director referred to Kejati Kaltim, Nov 2025 (pajak.go.id).
- Historical baseline: BPK recorded 525 fictitious-invoice cases 2016–2017, Rp1.01 trillion potential loss (hukumonline.com) — shows this is a chronic, not one-off, pattern.
candidates.killTest:
- **K1 Data access — PASS.** Buyer holds the invoices it receives and can query Coretax NPWP/PKP validation plus AHU/OSS licensing lookups without the counterparty's cooperation. No unified shell-detection API exists, but the needed inputs are self-obtainable.
- **K2 Oracle bound — PASS.** TBTS-ness leaves inferable traces: invoice-to-delivery mismatch, price/volume anomalies, geographic/network clustering of issuers (the "one village" pattern DJP found), rapid formation-dissolution cycles. DJP's own graph-analytics use confirms these signals are extractable.
- **K3 Absorption — PASS (no 12-month evidence found).** Coretax validates existence/format and DJP runs its own audit-targeting models, but neither warns buyers pre-transaction before they claim input credit — no roadmap or vendor announcement for that buyer-facing function was found.
- **K4 Bootstrap bar — PASS (weak-mixed confidence).** A self-serve, per-lookup or subscription API sold to finance/AP teams, or embedded into existing e-Faktur SaaS (B2B2B via Mekari/OnlinePajak/Pajakku, or KAP resale), is plausible without an enterprise-sales org, similar to existing self-serve KYB APIs (e.g., Kredibel) in Indonesia. ACV/count remain inferred, not directly evidenced.

**Survives: yes (all four pass, K4 on weak-mixed evidence).**
candidates.scores:
- Severity 7 — recurring documented state-loss prosecutions (Rp170B, Rp180B) plus criminal exposure under Pasal 39A create dedicated consultant/staff spend, but no confirmed buyer insolvency events.
- Bootstrap revenue 5 — plausible named segment, but ACV/count rest on analogy, not a directly cited comparable product price.
- WTP 6 — buyers already pay consultants (MUC, RSM, SW) for manual versions of this check; budget exists but is not consolidated around a single owned line item.
- Data position 5 — Coretax/AHU/OSS lookups are largely commodity, same-feed-to-anyone; some uplift possible from cross-customer pattern accumulation.
- Absorption distance 5 — DJP is visibly active in this exact space (AI/graph analytics) even though not buyer-facing; a plausible absorber with no confirmed roadmap.
- Competition 5 — Mekari/OnlinePajak/Pajakku sit adjacent with basic validity checks; none purpose-built for risk scoring, but the adjacency is real.
- Moat 5 — integration into a buyer's AP/tax workflow creates moderate switching cost; no cross-customer network effect confirmed.
- **Weighted: 5.6**
candidates.whatWouldKill: Coretax or a DJP-linked service publicly launching a pre-transaction counterparty risk score for buyers (flips K3); or Mekari/OnlinePajak/Pajakku shipping a proprietary shell-company risk-scoring feature into their existing e-Faktur products.

sources.raw: DDTC News (news.ddtc.co.id, various 2025–2026 TBTS case reports); pajak.go.id case releases (Jan 2026, Dec 2025, Nov 2025); investor.id (Jan 2026); Kontan/pajaknow.id ("desa" syndicate, 2026); hukumonline.com (BPK 2016–17 baseline); muc.co.id and Enforce A (buyer-side risk guidance); Mekari, OnlinePajak, Pajakku product pages; pajak.com/satvika.co.id (DJP AI use); DDTC (SE-8/PJ/2026, PMK-28/2026 risk-based compliance).

candidates.killReason: Below bar; Coretax/AHU/OSS inputs are same-feed commodity, ACV inferred by analogy to unpriced Mekari/OnlinePajak tiers.

searchIndex.text: ## Hard rules, learned expensively

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: Three prior research programs screened 121 candidates and produced two frozen

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: negative results. These rules are the residue. Violating them repeats months

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: of work.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: 1. **Never start from his capabilities.** The single most repeated failure in

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: this project was: *"he is good at deterministic replay, therefore build a

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: replay tool."* That reasoning is unfalsifiable — every domain contains

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: something unmeasured — and it produced four dead proposals. Start from a

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: documented operational problem that someone actually has. Map to his

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: strengths only *after* the problem is established, and say plainly when the

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: mapping is weak.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: 2. **Public evidence is biased.** Most software that is actually used is

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: private, and deals happen through relationships. GitHub issue counts are a

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: sample of what people rebuild *in public*, not what they rebuild. Weight

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: engineering blogs, postmortems, incident writeups, job postings, conference

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: talks and practitioner threads above issue counts. Say "(unverified)" when

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: you cannot source something.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: 3. **Apply these kill tests. Any failure eliminates.**

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - **K1 — fixable in six months?** If the incumbent, an upstream maintainer,

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: or a foundation could ship this as a feature in two quarters, it is a

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: feature gap, not a project. Demand a reason why fixing it is *against

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: their interest* or structurally hard, not merely unprioritised.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - **K2 — single beneficiary.** One team must get value alone, without

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: needing a second organisation to adopt anything. Standards efforts and

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: interchange formats die here; three years of prior attempts in this space

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: died exactly there.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - **K3 — solo-buildable.** One engineer ships something credible in ~3

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: months and can maintain it part-time for years. Anything needing a team,

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: sustained paid multi-provider archive access, or significant capex is out.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - **K4 — real practitioner pain, evidenced.** At least one named, dated

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: source of someone who operates this in production describing the problem.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: Not a vendor blog. Not your inference.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: 4. **The blockchain-necessity test, run in both directions.**

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - *"If blockchain disappeared tomorrow, would this project still make

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: sense?"* If **yes**, it is not a blockchain project — it is a general

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: tool, and it belongs in the other product.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - Then: *"Who specifically benefits because this is blockchain-native?"*

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: You must be able to name a concrete operator — a validator operator, a

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: rollup sequencer team, a bridge operator, a relayer, an oracle node

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: runner — not "the ecosystem."

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: ## Already eliminated — do not re-propose

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: A prior scout examined 25 blockchain infrastructure components. Rejected, with

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: reasons that still hold as of July 2026:

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - **Saturated:** multi-upstream RPC gateways (eRPC, dRPC, proxyd, PATH — you

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: would be entrant #11); wallet/key/account-abstraction infra (Privy, Turnkey,

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: Dynamic, Safe, Pimlico, ZeroDev, Fireblocks).

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - **Report, not a tool:** indexer conformance suites, cross-engine benchmark

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: suites. Nobody installs a report.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - **Needs vendor adoption (K2):** cross-fuzzer corpus interchange formats.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - **Capex-bound (K3):** cross-provider RPC correctness auditing, archive-node

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: cost work, anything needing recurring paid multi-provider access.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - **Upstream is shipping it (K1):** fork-cache reproducibility — Foundry ships

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: caching free as the CI default. A related idea, `forkprint` (offline

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: state-root-verifiable fork fixtures), was specced and then killed; its

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: evidence was two GitHub issues and one blog post, which fails K4.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: - **Weak demand for the adjacent product:** independent verification of indexed

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: on-chain data. The structural argument is the strongest anyone found — the

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: product's output measures the vendor's own error rate, so shipping it invites

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: liability — but **nobody sells verification at any price.** Demand for

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: indexing is not demand for indexing-verification. Treat this as a cautionary

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: pattern, not an opportunity.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: ## One hypothesis worth testing, not assuming

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: Protocol operators run infrastructure and have on-call problems that generic

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: tools serve badly: missed block proposals, sequencer stalls, bridge liveness,

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: relayer failures, oracle heartbeat gaps, validator slashing risk. The operator

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: is a single team (K2 passes), the pain is operational and dated, and the domain

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: knowledge is not general SRE knowledge.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: **Test it, do not assume it.** Two honest objections you must address:

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: integration work is shallow engineering and makes a weak portfolio piece; and

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: several monitoring vendors already serve this. If your investigation says the

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: hard part is genuinely hard — consensus-aware state, correct liveness

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: detection under reorgs, distinguishing "the chain is slow" from "our node is

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: broken" — say so with evidence. If it says the hard part is writing API

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: clients, kill it and look elsewhere.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: ## What to produce

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: 1. **Two weeks of investigation, maximum, then stop.** Prior programs

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: overspent on desk research; the failure mode is researching forever.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: 2. A short findings document: candidates examined, K1–K4 verdicts, and the

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: evidence behind each — sources named and dated.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: 3. **One selected project**, with: the operational problem in one sentence; who

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: has it, by name; why existing tools fail them; the architecture; the *hard*

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: engineering problem at its centre; and a **pre-registered benchmark** —

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: what is measured, against which baseline, and what result counts as failure,

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: written down before implementation.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: 4. **Then build it.** Working, tested code beats another document. The user has

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: said this repeatedly and is right. Ship a v0 that a practitioner could run,

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: not a scaffold.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: ## Standing evidence rules

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: No number without a named source and year, else mark it "(unverified)".

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: Several secondary sources repeating one figure count as one source. Check the

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: competitive state at the time you recommend, not from memory — this space moves

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: in months. Report what would kill the idea, not only what would make it work.

searchIndex.title: Brief for a separate Claude Code agent — blockchain infrastructure portfolio project
searchIndex.text: When you are wrong, say so plainly and continue.

searchIndex.text: ## Implications for Phase 2

searchIndex.title: CROSSCUT — Trust-Failure Patterns Across the 30-Industry Scan
searchIndex.text: 1. **Genuinely horizontal (one buyer type, one workflow):** CRED (verify-side), DUP (lender-facing financial subset). These are the only two where "platform" is honest on day one.

searchIndex.title: CROSSCUT — Trust-Failure Patterns Across the 30-Industry Scan
searchIndex.text: 2. **Horizontal failure, vertical product — pick one wedge:** PROV (split minerals vs smallholder; minerals is where both kill-test survivors sit), AUTH (pharma first), EVT (JKN slice only), DOC (pick one issuer), SETT (logistics only).

searchIndex.title: CROSSCUT — Trust-Failure Patterns Across the 30-Industry Scan
searchIndex.text: 3. **Anti-candidates as platforms:** COLL (verification doesn't bind colluders), ID (served market), FUND (no willing buyer without per-sector mandates).

searchIndex.title: CROSSCUT — Trust-Failure Patterns Across the 30-Industry Scan
searchIndex.text: 4. **Scoring hygiene:** re-check any weighted score whose severity evidence is dominated by COLL-type cases before advancing it.

searchIndex.text: ## 3. Verdict on the premise

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: **The Indonesian negative result is not caused by Indonesian market structure.

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: It reproduces elsewhere — and the mechanism of reproduction is not the one

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: Program B named.**

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: Two things must be separated cleanly.

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: **What *is* Indonesia-specific.** Two of Program B's stated failure terms are

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: genuine artefacts of Indonesian market thinness and do reverse abroad. Buyer

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: count reverses in six of nine cases, sometimes by two orders of magnitude

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: (1.53 crore GSTINs vs 150–250 Indonesian PKP finance teams). Price

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: observability reverses in six of nine — Indonesia's "no observable price"

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: finding (§6 of the conclusion) is substantially a small-market artefact.

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: **What is not.** In every case where those two terms reversed, the candidate

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: still failed, because the binding constraint was never buyer count or price

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: *visibility*. It was price *level*, incumbent density, and above all the sales

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: **motion** — gate G6. Seven of the nine die at least partly on G6; the pattern

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: is remorselessly consistent. In developed markets, higher willingness to pay

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: is *purchased with* procurement: a BAA, SOC 2, vendor security review, model

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: risk documentation. Every ACV large enough to reach $1M ARR with a reachable

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: customer count sits behind that wall, and every tier that is genuinely

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: self-serve has been commoditised to $0.33–$14 per transaction by funded

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: vendors. That is the structural finding, and it is general, not Indonesian.

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: One correction to the frozen record's *interpretation* (not its verdict):

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: Program B read the free state substitute as an Indonesian pathology. **It is

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: not.** UK Companies House serves the register free by API; GSTN's IMS gives

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: Indian buyers per-invoice reject rights free; RBI distributes MuleHunter.AI

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: free to 23 banks; SSA's eCBSV is statutory and cheap; NPDB is $2.50; MSPO

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: Trace is free and mandatory. Richer states ship *more* free substitution, not

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: less. Program B's §6 conclusion holds; its implied geographic explanation does

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: not.

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: So the honest formulation: **the constraint is partly Indonesia-specific, and

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: the founder constraint bites just as hard elsewhere — harder.** A bigger

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: market bought bigger incumbents and a heavier sale, not an easier one.

searchIndex.text: ## 5. Limits

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: Desk research, one pass, no customer interviews — the same standard as

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: Programs A and B, with less rigour, since no protocol governed it. Several

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: The largest unmeasured term is not in the table. **A solo remote Indonesian

searchIndex.text: founder selling into US, UK or EU regulated buyers faces trust, procurement,

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: data-residency, contracting and payment friction that this note cannot

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B
searchIndex.text: assumes that friction is zero. It is not zero, and it runs in one direction

searchIndex.title: Geography Note — Appendix to Program B

searchIndex.text: **Purpose: falsify desk research, not validate an idea.** Programs A and B

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide

searchIndex.text: ## The rule

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: **Do not pitch. Do not describe a product.** The moment you describe a

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: solution, the interview stops producing evidence and starts producing

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: politeness. Ask what they did last time, not what they would do.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: If asked what you're building: *"Nothing yet — I'm researching how

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: [credential checks / fraud losses / claims disputes] actually work before I

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: decide whether to build anything."* That is true, and it keeps the data

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: clean.
