searchIndex.text: ## Who to talk to

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: **Group 1 — buyers in the two best-evidenced pain areas** (~10 people).

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: These are where the corpus has real documented losses and at least one real

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: price, so being wrong is most detectable:

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: - Private hospital HR / credentialing staff, and the medical committee

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: member who signs off (`credential-holder-identity-binding`; MedTrack sells

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: here at Rp250–350k/month, so budget exists).

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: - BPR / BPD internal audit and compliance heads (`bpr-insider-fraud-continuous-audit`;

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: SI-INSAF Rp2.6M per bank via Perbarindo, SAF-GEN Rp6.9–9.9M/month).

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: **Group 2 — the sales-motion reality check** (~5 people). Anyone who sells

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: software into Indonesian regulated buyers.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: **Interview 0 — do this one first, before any buyer.** The friend who

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: already sells SaaS to government and similar organisations. It is not

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Interview 1 in a sequence; it is a different question entirely, and its

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: answer changes how every later interview should be read. Its purpose is not

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: to validate a candidate — it is to estimate whether G6 reflects reality for

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: *these* circumstances. If it turns out that channel partners routinely carry

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: third-party software, that deals close in weeks rather than many months, and

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: that procurement is lighter than the corpus assumes, then the buyer

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: interviews are being run against a constraint that is looser than modelled.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: If it confirms the corpus, you know before spending twenty conversations

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: that G6 remains dominant. Questions in "The G6 question" below.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: **Group 3 — one or two people who tried and stopped.** Founders or product

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: managers from any incumbent named in the corpus. What they learned from

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: failing is worth more than what a happy customer says.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: ## What to attack

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Five written assumptions, each with the question that tests it. Every one

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: was inferred from desk sources and could be wrong.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: **A1 — The pain is real and owned.** *Corpus says:* documented fraud,

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: dedicated staff, real losses.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Ask: "Walk me through the last time a [fake credential / insider fraud /

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: disputed claim] actually happened here. What did you do that week? Who found

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: it?" — If nobody can recall an instance, severity scoring across the corpus

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: is too high.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: **A2 — Someone owns a budget line.** *Corpus says:* named budget owners

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: already pay for inferior alternatives.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Ask: "What do you currently spend on this — software, staff time, an

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: external auditor? Who signs that off?" — Then: "When did that budget last

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: change, and why?"

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: **A3 — The free state substitute is actually used.** *This is the assumption

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: most likely to be wrong, and it kills the most candidates.* The corpus

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: concluded that free state tools (SATUSEHAT, VIBI, Berbagi Akses, SIVIL,

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: automatic PKKPR) close the gap.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Ask: "Do you use [the state system]? For what, exactly? What do you still do

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: manually or outside it?" — If regulated buyers describe state tools as

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: unusable, incomplete, or ignored in practice, then a whole class of K3

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: absorption kills was wrong on the ground while being right on paper. **This

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: is the single most valuable question in this guide.**

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: **A4 — Price level.** *Corpus says:* observed prices are an order of

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: magnitude below bootstrap economics.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Ask: "If something removed this problem entirely, what would that be worth

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: per year to you?" — then shut up. Do not suggest a number.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: **A5 — Sales motion (G6).** *Corpus says:* every ACV large enough is gated

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: behind procurement and security review, which a solo founder cannot run.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Ask: "How did you buy the last new software tool? How long did it take, who

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: had to approve it, and was there a security or vendor review?" — If small

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: tools genuinely get bought on a card by a department head, G6 is less

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: binding than the corpus assumes.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: ## The G6 question

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: After 86 candidates and nine geography memos, **G6 — product-led adoption

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: only, no enterprise sales motion — is the constraint that binds.** State it

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: precisely, because the precise version is the stronger claim: G6 does not

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: kill companies, it *defines the set of companies this search ran over*.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Programs A and B did not show that enterprise integrity software is not

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: worth building. They showed that **among companies compatible with this

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: founder model, none was found.** The geography test sharpened it further —

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: richer markets did not relieve G6, they tightened it.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: G6 is a choice, not a fact about the world. It was pre-committed for good

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: reasons (solo, employment alongside, side-project survivability). Knowing it

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: is the binding term is what makes the next conversation worth having.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: So one conversation matters more than the other nineteen. With the

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: SaaS-selling friend, establish:

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: 1. Who exactly do they sell to — which agency, institution or company type,

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: by name, not "government"?

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: 2. What is a real closed contract size and how long did it take?

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: 3. What did the buyer require — PT, NIB, e-katalog listing, security review,

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: references, prior deployments?

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: 4. What was actually paid, and how many months after signature?

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: 5. Would they carry a product they did not build, and on what split?

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Under the channel-partner rule (`CONTEXT.md`, 2026-07-29), this only ever

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: counts if the friend already sells to a candidate's *specific* buyer type,

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: with dependencies logged first. But the answers change which constraint is

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: binding — and that is worth knowing before deciding this search is over.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: ## A6 — the last question, and possibly the best one

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: End every interview in Group 1 with this, exactly as written:

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: > **"What software did you buy last year that surprised you?"**

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Not "what integrity software." Not "what fraud tools." Just what they

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: bought. This is a **budget-first search run inside a problem-first

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: interview** — and budget-first is the direction both frozen conclusions name

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: as the most promising unexplored one.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: If several buyers independently name something that appears nowhere in 86

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: candidate files, that is worth more than confirming any assumption above:

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: it means the sourcing process systematically missed a whole spending

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: category. Record the answer verbatim, even when it sounds irrelevant.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: *Especially* when it sounds irrelevant.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: ## What would count as a surprise

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Write these down before starting, so hindsight cannot rewrite them. Any one

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: of these is a real result:

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: - Buyers describe the free state substitute as unusable in practice (A3).

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: - A buyer names a number for A4 more than 5× the corpus's observed prices.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: - Small tools are routinely bought without procurement or security review

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: (A5) — G6 is looser than assumed.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: - Someone volunteers a pain, unprompted, that appears nowhere in 86

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: candidate files. **Look hard for this one**: both programs sourced

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: problem-first, and the corpus's own recommendation is that a

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: *budget-first* search — start from what buyers already pay for, then find

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: the integrity slice — is the more promising unexplored direction.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: - Two or more buyers give the same A6 answer, and it is absent from the

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: corpus. That is the budget-first signal arriving unprompted.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: ## After the interviews

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Write up what was heard within 24 hours of each conversation, before it

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: blurs. Then one honest page: which of A1–A5 survived, which broke, and

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: whether anything heard would have changed a kill-test verdict in the frozen

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: matrices.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: If nothing broke, the frozen conclusions stand and this search is genuinely

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: finished. If A3 or A5 broke, that is grounds to open a new versioned

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: program — with a pre-registered protocol, per `PROGRAM-B-CONCLUSION.md` §10.

searchIndex.title: Buyer Interview Guide
searchIndex.text: Not to reopen A or B.

searchIndex.text: # Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: **Pre-committed 2026-07-30, before any candidate was examined.** New program.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: Inherits nothing from Programs A and B except their negative constraints and

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: their evidence discipline. Both remain frozen.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: ## Why the previous rubric was wrong

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: Programs A and B scored **competition as a negative** — anchor 9 was "verified

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: whitespace", anchor 3 was "funded incumbents with traction". In a functioning

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: market that is backwards: an empty room usually means nobody wants the thing.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: 86 candidates were screened for empty rooms and the result was reported as a

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: finding that the rooms were empty.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: Competition answers the hardest question in the whole search — *does anyone

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: actually pay for this?* Program C therefore treats incumbents as **evidence**,

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: and asks the question that follows: **why has no incumbent taken the whole

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: market, and why are customers still unhappy?**

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: ## Question

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: > Find a software category with **proven spending**, establish **why paying

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: > customers remain dissatisfied**, identify a **structural** reason incumbents

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: > cannot fix it, and specify an implementation whose advantage can be

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: > **measured**.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: Blockchain, government, Indonesia and AI are candidate *domains*, not the

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: objective.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: ## Unit of analysis

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: An **existing product people pay for** — not a problem, not an industry. Every

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: candidate starts from a named incumbent with an observed price.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: ## Scoring (two independent axes, never summed)

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: **Demand Proof (0–10)** — 0: nobody buying. 3: niche buying. 7: multiple

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: healthy vendors with published prices. 10: large, documented, recurring spend.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: **Displacement Opportunity** — assessed only for candidates with Demand

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: Proof ≥ 5. Scored on whether the dissatisfaction has a **structural** cause:

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: - priced for enterprise, cannot profitably serve the small end

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: - architecture makes the missing capability slow or expensive to add

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: - support, language or region gap the incumbent won't staff

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: - incentives favour existing large customers over a new use case

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: - complexity is the *price* of serving very large organisations

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: - technical debt or a business-model constraint (licensing, usage pricing)

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: ## Kill tests (any failure eliminates)

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: 1. **Fixable-in-six-months.** If the incumbent could ship this as a feature in

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: two quarters, it is a feature gap, not a displacement. **Kill.**

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: 2. **Single-buyer.** One organisation must be able to buy it, deploy it, and

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: benefit from it *alone*. Anything requiring two organisations to cooperate

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: has no budget owner. (Derived from Programs A and B: nearly every candidate

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: that died was a network, registry, or interop play.) **Kill if it needs a

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: network.**

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: 3. **Solo-buildable wedge.** One engineer ships a credible v1 in ~3 months.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: **Kill if it needs a team to be credible at all.**

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: 4. **Evidenced complaint.** At least one *paying customer* complaint from a

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: review site, forum, migration post, or public thread. **GitHub issues alone

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: do not count** — public code artefacts are a biased sample of practice, and

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: most software that is actually used is private.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: ## Evidence rules

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: Named source and date for every price, complaint and claim, else

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: "(unverified)". Preferred evidence, in order: published pricing pages; review

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: platforms (G2, Capterra, TrustRadius); "why we migrated off X" engineering

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: posts; support forums and feature-request boards; practitioner threads. Several

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: sources repeating one claim count as one.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: ## Founder advantages this program may legitimately price in

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: - **Price floor.** Derived bars are $6k / $15k / $60k per year

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: (`BAR-SENSITIVITY-NOTE.md`). A customer worth $500/year is unprofitable for a

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: vendor with a sales team and fine for a solo operator. This is a structural

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: advantage, not a consolation.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: - **Locale.** Indonesian language, regulation and integrations are too small a

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: market for a global vendor to staff and large enough for one person.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: - **Distribution.** One named channel relationship into Indonesian government

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: and enterprise buyers (`CONTEXT.md`, channel-partner rule still applies).

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: ## Output

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: Not a rejection matrix. A ranked set of **displacement hypotheses**, each with:

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: incumbent and observed price; cited customer complaints; the structural root

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: cause; why the incumbent cannot fix it; the architectural change that would;

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: the segment served first; and a **pre-registered benchmark** — what is measured,

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: against which baseline, and what result would count as failure.

searchIndex.title: Program C Protocol — Displacement, not whitespace
searchIndex.text: Then one is built.

searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: Indonesian retail savers buy fractional "digital gold" through apps (Pluang, Treasury, IndoGold, Lakuemas, Pegadaian's Tabungan Emas/Tring). searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: Retail savers bear the ultimate risk but cannot pay for attestation. Licensed pedagang emas digital (roughly five to seven firms) pay depository, clearing, and exchange fees — they are the only plausible buyers of an attestation product. Depositories and clearing houses do the physical verification

The failure occurred *outside* the license

searchIndex.text: - Antam branded-gold case: prosecutions concluded in 2025 over 109 tonnes of gold improperly stamped with Antam's brand by insiders between 2010 and 2021 (Indonesian court proceedings, 2025; Phase 1 anchor). This is a provenance/branding failure at the state refiner, adjacent to but distinct from pl

searchIndex.text: - China digital-gold platform collapse, 2025–2026 (external): retail investors lost billions of yuan on unredeemable digital gold (Kumparan, 2026). searchIndex.text: - Within the licensed depository regime since 2023: no documented backing shortfall found in this search, repeated in July 2026 — (none found).

searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: Digital physical gold transactions reached Rp 53.3 trillion (43.9 tonnes) in January–November 2024, up 556% from Rp 8.1 trillion in the same period of 2023 (Bappebti via Tempo, 2024). searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - State custody chain: 1:1 physical deposit at ICDX Logistik Berikat or Kinesis Monetary Indonesia, max 20% cash at KBI/ICH clearing, Bappebti supervision (Kontan, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - Kinesis Monetary Indonesia: a blockchain-based gold platform that is itself an approved depository operator — the "tokenized, auditable gold" slot already exists inside the regulated ecosystem.

searchIndex.text: - Bullion banks: Pegadaian and BSI under direct OJK prudential supervision, with Pegadaian's Tring app as a licensed retail channel (Pegadaian, 2025). The national program was launched by President Prabowo on 26 February 2025; OJK remains open to further bullion-bank applicants, and as of September

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - Globally: LBMA chain-of-custody standards; tokenized gold products (PAXG, XAUT) — not Indonesia-licensed retail channels.

searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient & Who Rejects the Existing Anchor

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: Nobody economically relevant rejects the anchor. Retail savers trust the Bappebti/OJK license badge (the Tamasia lesson as reported domestically was "check the license," not "demand independent proof"). Platforms accept depository and clearing oversight as their cost of doing business. Banks lending

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: Multi-org in form (platform, depository, clearing, regulator), but the state-supervised clearing house is an accepted neutral party performing exactly the reconciliation a chain would do. Kinesis already offers blockchain-native gold inside the licensed perimeter, and it has not become the trust sta

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain? YES — unbacked gold claims predate crypto (Tamasia). PASS.

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a single trusted operator? YES — the depository-plus-clearing ledger under Bappebti/OJK is accepted by all parties. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: 3. State/incumbent ships it in six months? Already shipped — the 1:1 depository mandate is in force; OJK's bullion regime extends it. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone company value? NO — under ten licensed platform buyers plus two bullion banks. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: Killed, consistent with H1: an accepted state anchor occupies the slot.

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 5 — real consumer harm documented (Tamasia, 2023) but confined to the unlicensed fringe; licensed regime clean so far.

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - Market 3 — attestation TAM spans <10 platforms and 2 bullion banks despite Rp 53.3T flows; well under $50M.

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 4 — platforms already pay depository/clearing fees and treat them as sufficient; no budget for a second layer.

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 4 — accepted trusted intermediaries (KBI/ICH + approved depositories) exist; multi-org but anchored.

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 4 — 556% growth and bullion-bank rollout raise scrutiny, but no deadline or fresh licensed-regime scandal.

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 3 — Kinesis (blockchain gold, funded, inside the ecosystem) and state infrastructure occupy the space.

searchIndex.title: Digital Gold Custody — Backing Attestation (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 3 — attestation over a state-run custody chain is a copyable feature.

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: An Indonesian fisheries exporter today runs a document relay across at least four authorities. Step by step: (1) vessel >20 GT lands catch at a fisheries port; port authority (KKP Ditjen Perikanan Tangkap) issues the SHTI catch certificate (Lembar Awal, then Lembar Turunan for EU-bound consignments)

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: Domestic side: exporters/UPIs pay PNBP fees per certificate plus logistics dwell; KKP, Barantin, Bea Cukai and LNSW (Kemenkeu) do the work; BPK audits; exporters and forwarders dispute delays. Foreign side: the EU Commission (DG MARE/DG SANTE) validates SHTI and health certificates flag-state-to-por

searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: The fragmentation is real but the failure mode is friction, not contested truth. Documented: overlapping quality certification after the BKIPM split — SMKHP (KKP) duplicating checks feeding KI-1 (Barantin), acknowledged by both agencies and addressed by PP 25/2025 task division and a joint electroni

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: Fisheries exports were USD 6.27B in 2025, up 5.2%, with the US at USD 1.99B (31.8%), China USD 1.22B, EU USD 451.7M (KKP, January 2026). Friction cost: SSm QC container dwell time averaged 3.31 days against a 3.23-day SLA in July 2022 (LNSW, 2022); per-shipment excess cost of the residual multi-agen

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: State: INSW/SSm QC joint inspection (14 ports, expanding); e-SHTI issuance at fishing ports; Stelina (KKP national fish traceability/logistics system); Barantin–BPPMHKP electronic certificate integration piloting July 2026; KKP–BP Batam agreement (23 July 2026) linking KKP certification with the IBO

searchIndex.text: Remaining gaps: agency systems still reconcile bilaterally (the July 2026 pilot proves integration is unfinished); small-vessel catch data below 20 GT is thin, limiting SIMP/EU traceability depth. But no economically relevant party rejects the anchor. Exporters want INSW to work, not to be replaced;

searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: Multi-org, single accepted intermediary already mandated (INSW). Tamper-evidence changes no behavior: certificates are distrusted for content (was the fish really that vessel's catch?), which a ledger cannot attest — only observers, logbooks and port inspectors can. Chain necessity ~2/10.

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED (H1 prediction confirmed)

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain? YES — pure inter-agency workflow.

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under one trusted operator? YES — INSW is precisely that, and both sides of the border accept it (foreign verifiers accept the state anchor by treaty). FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: 3. State ships it in six months? It is shipping now: SSm QC since 2022, PP 25/2025, SMKHP–KI-1 integration pilot July 2026. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone company value? Documentation-brokering SaaS against a free, mandated state platform — no. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: - Market 4 — compliance-software slice of a USD 6.27B export flow, realistically sub-$50–100M (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: - WTP 4 — exporters pay fees but expect clearance to be a free public service; budget owner is the state.

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: - Chain 2 — mandated accepted intermediary exists; foreign verifiers accept flag-state certificates.

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 4 — pressure is declining as integrations land; no external deadline forcing change.

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: - Competition 3 — INSW is a funded incumbent with a presidential mandate; traceability pilots crowd the rest.

searchIndex.title: Multi-Agency Fisheries Export Clearance — AXIS 5-CONTROL
searchIndex.text: - Moat 3 — any integration layer is displaced the day INSW ships the same connection.

searchIndex.text: # Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: An Indonesian mutual fund (reksa dana) is run by an investment manager (manajer investasi, MI) but its assets sit at a custodian bank, which by design is the party that computes the daily net asset value (NAV/NAB) using OJK's standard formula — the manager does not price its own fund (SEOJK 1/SEOJK.

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: 26 commercial banks are registered custodians (Pintu, 2024); the largest, HSBC Indonesia, held Rp976.13 trillion in custody as of September 2023 (Pintu, 2023). Custody fees of roughly 0.1–0.25% of AUM are embedded in NAV (Pintu, 2024 — approximate). ~90 licensed MIs pay S-INVEST usage fees to KSEI.

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (cited incidents)

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - **Jiwasraya**: BPK's investigative audit put state losses at Rp16.81 trillion — Rp4.65 trillion from equities and Rp12.16 trillion from mutual funds used as wrappers for manipulated, illiquid stocks (BPK, 2020).

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - **Asabri**: Rp22.78 trillion in state losses, 2012–2019, through arranged placements in stocks and mutual funds tied to the manipulators (BPK, 2021).

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - **Minna Padi AM**: OJK dissolved 6 funds worth Rp5.72 trillion AUM that promised "guaranteed" 11% returns (OJK/CNBC Indonesia, 2019).

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - **Narada AM**: suspended after failing to pay Rp177.78 billion for stock purchases (OJK/Bisnis, 2019).

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - **Kresna AM**: 24 funds suspended by OJK (August 2020).

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - **Custodian layer**: OJK found NAV miscalculations, late NAV reporting, and weak valuation oversight, ordering corrective action at 11 custodian banks and compliance exams at 3 (Bisnis.com, 2020).

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - **Underlying assets**: SNP Finance's fictitious and double-pledged receivables backed Rp1.85 trillion of MTN that defaulted in 2018 (Tirto/Bisnis, 2018), poisoning portfolios that held them.

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - In February 2026 Bareskrim named suspects for mutual-fund price manipulation: two Narada AM executives (president commissioner and a director) and three at Minna Padi AM; underlying stocks came from projects controlled by insiders via affiliates and nominees. Roughly Rp674 billion of client funds

searchIndex.text: Industry NAB was Rp652.90 trillion (~US$40B) at end-June 2026, down 3.32% year-to-date and 4.79% month-on-month (OJK RDK press release, June 2026); it stood at Rp726.26 trillion in February and Rp685.76 trillion in May 2026 (OJK, 2026) — an industry in outflow, not growth. searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - **KSEI S-INVEST** — the state-mandated shared system of record for the entire fund industry since 2016.

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - **Custodian banks** as regulated independent NAV calculators, with SEOJK 1/2015 error-correction procedure.

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: - **OJK reform program** — post-2020 supervision tightening continuing into 2026 (Bareksa, May 2026).

searchIndex.text: - **DLT infrastructure**: Calastone Tokenised Distribution integrated with Polygon, November 2025; OJK sandbox graduates in tokenization (Blocktogo gold, Nano's KPD securities tokenization, GORO property — OJK sandbox, 2025). None target NAV attestation.

searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient & Who Rejects the Existing Anchor

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: The honest answer: no economically relevant party rejects the anchor. Foreign sub-custodians clear through KSEI; institutional investors accept OJK-supervised custodian NAVs; courts accept BPK audits. Every major loss occurred through collusion or valuation fraud inside the perimeter — manipulated p

searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: If blockchain disappeared, the problem (valuation fraud, weak custodian oversight) persists — pass. But a single trusted operator's database already exists and is accepted by all parties: S-INVEST literally is that PostgreSQL, run by KSEI — fail. OJK/KSEI can extend it by regulation within months, a

searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Fund NAV and custody attestation (axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: **KILLED.** Fails kill tests #2 and #3. The customer problem is real (#1 passes) but the accepted neutral operator exists, and incumbents/state can ship the remedy. Standalone economics (#4) also doubtful once collusion losses are stripped.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: Halal certification has no global anchor: each importing country's religious-regulatory authority decides whose certificates count. Outbound: an Indonesian exporter certified by BPJPH (with MUI fatwa, audited by an LPH such as LPPOM MUI, Sucofindo, or Surveyor Indonesia) must still satisfy the desti

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: Indonesian side: BPJPH (Kemenag) as certifier-regulator, MUI as fatwa authority, competing LPHs as auditors, exporters (food and beverage is 81% of halal exports), and importers/distributors of foreign goods facing the 2026 deadline. Foreign side: JAKIM (Malaysia), MUIS (Singapore), Saudi Halal Cent

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - 2023: the Nabidz case — a wine carried a genuine BPJPH certificate obtained through the no-lab-audit self-declare channel by submitting the product as grape juice; BPJPH revoked it effective 15 August 2023 after finding the application data manipulated (BPJPH, 2023; Tempo, 2023).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - 2024: BPJPH revoked the halal certificate of Roti Okko after finding production non-conformities and an unregistered variant carrying the halal label (BPJPH, August 2024).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - April 2025: BPOM and BPJPH announced nine processed foods — mostly imported marshmallows — testing positive for porcine DNA/peptides, seven holding valid halal certificates; BPJPH ordered withdrawal (BPOM press release, 21 April 2025). In June 2025 LPPOM MUI's re-tests came back negative, publicly

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Regionally, Malaysia's December 2020 scandal — a cartel that for ~40 years bribed officials to pass uncertified imported meat (including kangaroo and horse) as halal (Arab News, 2021) — is the reference case importing regulators cite for distrusting exporter-side paperwork.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Fake or self-claimed halal logos are widespread on marketplaces, with no public digital label verification distinguishing genuine marks (LPH BMS, 2025; Kompas, 2023 on sanctions).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Cross-border, the failure is institutional distrust rather than forgery: each authority re-audits because it does not accept the other's standard (stunning rules, slaughter method, HAS 23000 vs MS1500 vs GSO 2055-1 divergence).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Indonesia's halal product exports: $41.4B January–October 2024 (Kemendag via Antara, 2024); full-year 2024 figures of $64.11B (Deputy Industry Minister via VOI, 2025) and total halal trade of $53.73B (Kemendag, 2024) circulate — figures conflict, treat magnitudes only.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Avoided re-certification cost when an MRA path exists: $700–2,500 per certificate (halalregistration.com, 2026 — commercial source).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Per-market audit and renewal costs for exporters across JAKIM/SHC/MoIAT tracks: (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Domestic mandatory-certification compliance spend after October 2026: large but state-captured via BPJPH tariffs; (unverified) at aggregate level.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - BPJPH's MRA program: 52 mutual recognition agreements with foreign halal bodies across 24 countries, with new signings through May 2026 (Morocco, Italy, France, South Korea, China) (BPJPH via Emerhub; Antara, 2026).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Indonesia–Malaysia MoC on mutual recognition of BPJPH/JAKIM certificates (BPJPH, 2025; exact scope limited to domestic products of each country).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - SHLN foreign-certificate registration under BPJPH Decree 221/2025.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - SMIIC standards and the International Halal Accreditation Forum for multilateral convergence.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Private tech: OneAgrix with OriginTrail blockchain certificate verification (Singapore, since 2019); Verify Halal (Serunai, Malaysia); numerous Indonesian academic blockchain-traceability pilots (MDPI 2022–2025), none at commercial scale.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - BPJPH public certificate-check database (halal.go.id).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient & Who Rejects the Existing Anchor

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: This is the cleanest H1 pattern of the three: no single institution is accepted by every economically relevant party. Saudi Arabia's Halal Center does not accept a BPJPH certificate as sufficient; BPJPH does not accept unregistered foreign certificates; Malaysia and Indonesia only bridged their sche

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: Adversarial sovereign parties plus external verifiers exist, but tamper-evidence does not change behavior: a cryptographically immutable BPJPH certificate is still rejected by Riyadh if the slaughterhouse used stunning. The binding constraint is being resolved by treaty (MRAs), which no ledger can s

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: 1. Without blockchain, does the problem persist? Yes. PASS.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: 2. Would PostgreSQL under a single trusted operator solve it? For authenticity, yes — each issuer's own database is accepted about its own certificates. For recognition, no database of any architecture solves it. FAIL (on the solvable part).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: 3. Can the state ship it in six months? Yes — BPJPH is shipping the fix by decree and MRA (Decree 221/2025; 52 MRAs). FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone economic value? Compliance value is large but flows to state fee schedules and accredited auditors; a private cross-border verification layer has no mandate to charge against. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 6 — duplicated audits per market and a 2025 certified-product contamination scandal; recurring cost and reputational exposure.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Market 5 — halal compliance services around $53–64B trade flows plausibly land in the $50–250M addressable band for tooling; recognition itself is not purchasable.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 6 — mandated compliance spend with a hard deadline, but budget owners pay BPJPH/LPHs and certifiers, not a neutral verifier.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 6 — genuinely no accepted neutral party across borders, but tamper-evidence does not change recognition behavior; discounted accordingly.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 8 — the import-certification deadline of 17 October 2026 is under three months away and enforcement follows immediately.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 5 — several attempts (OneAgrix, Verify Halal, pilots), none dominant; but the state occupies the center.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 5 — integration into MRA/SHLN workflows could lock in, but the standard-setting position belongs to states and SMIIC.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certificate Mutual Recognition Across Borders (halal-mutual-recognition, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Weighted: 5.8

searchIndex.text: It is killed as a blockchain-necessity play by the doctrinal nature of the dispute and the state's active MRA rollout. searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: An Indonesian nurse seeking work abroad holds an ijazah (D3/Ners degree), an STR registration (now lifetime, issued by Konsil Kesehatan Indonesia under Health Law 17/2023), and employer experience letters. Each destination re-verifies from scratch. Gulf corridor: every GCC health regulator (SCFHS Sa

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: Indonesian side: the nurse (who pays most fees), nursing schools and poltekkes, KKI/Kemenkes as registrar, KP2MI as placement authority, licensed placement agencies. Foreign side: Gulf regulators and their delegated verifier DataFlow; German Länder recognition offices, the Federal Employment Agency

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Bima, NTB, 2016: a district health office audit found hundreds of nurse STRs to be fake (Radar Lombok, 2016).

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Morotai, 2021: CPNS health-worker applicants were found using fake STRs from candidates who had never taken the competency exam (Tandaseru, 2021).

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Brokers ("calo") sell fake STRs for Rp1.5–2.5 million to candidates who repeatedly fail the competency exam (Merdeka, undated investigative feature).

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Gulf-side context: DataFlow reports having screened 375,000 GCC-bound doctors, nurses, and allied professionals since 2013 and flagged more than 10,000 fake or misrepresented credentials, with India and the Philippines accounting for 73% of detected fraud; Indonesia is not among the named top sour

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: This domestic fraud history is precisely why foreign regulators refuse to accept Indonesian paper at face value and mandate third-party PSV.

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Per-applicant verification cost: ~$255 DataFlow fee for Qatar (NEAC, 2026); apostille/translation costs (unverified, low hundreds of dollars).

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Delay cost: 25–45 working days standard, up to several months on unresponsive institutions (Allocation Assist, 2024) — borne as lost wages by the nurse and vacancy cost by the employer (unverified in money terms).

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Flow volumes are small: Japan EPA has placed 547 nurse candidates and 966 care-worker candidates since 2008 (Kemenkes); Germany's G-to-G Batch VII 2025 sought 150 nurses (KP2MI, 2025); Triple Win has placed 6,200+ nurses since inception across all partner countries, not just Indonesia (GIZ, 2024).

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - DataFlow Group: the entrenched, regulator-mandated PSV monopoly across all GCC health authorities, with cross-regulator "report transfer" portability (NEAC, 2026).

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Kemenkumham e-Apostille (since 2022) for document legalization.

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - KKI lifetime STR and Kemenkes SATUSEHAT/SISDMK registries domestically.

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - CGFNS for the US pathway; anabin database for German equivalence; JICWELS for Japan.

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - KP2MI/ILO/IOM accreditation system for placement agencies under development (IOM, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient & Who Rejects the Existing Anchor

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: Foreign regulators genuinely reject the Indonesian state anchor: GCC authorities will not license on an apostilled STR alone, and Germany re-assesses substance, not just authenticity. This matches H1's trigger condition on its face. But the market has already converged on accepted neutral intermedia

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: The parties are not adversarial custodians; they are slow registrars plus foreign regulators who have already appointed trusted intermediaries they accept. A custodian-independent ledger of Indonesian credentials would still require each Gulf regulator to accept it in place of DataFlow — there is no

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: 1. Without blockchain, does the problem persist? Yes. PASS.

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: 2. Would PostgreSQL under a single trusted operator solve it? Yes — DataFlow effectively is that operator for the Gulf, and it is acceptable to both sides. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: 3. Can an incumbent ship it in six months? Yes — DataFlow already offers report transfer and could extend corridors; Kemenkes could expose a registry API by decree. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone economic value? No — Indonesian outflow volumes put addressable verification spend in single-digit $M. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 5 — measurable cost and months of delay per nurse, but a functioning (if slow) path exists in every corridor.

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)
searchIndex.text: - Market 2 — low-thousands annual placements times ~$300 verification spend; far under $50M.

searchIndex.title: Foreign Verification of Indonesian Health-Worker Credentials (health-worker-mobility, axis 1)

searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Pre-Title Property Double-Selling (PPJB Layer) — axis 2B
searchIndex.text: Indonesian developers sell housing and apartment units before the title deed (AJB) can be executed, using the Perjanjian Pengikatan Jual Beli (PPJB). searchIndex.title: Pre-Title Property Double-Selling (PPJB Layer) — axis 2B
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Pre-Title Property Double-Selling (PPJB Layer) — axis 2B
searchIndex.text: Domestic only — no cross-border party. Buyers (consumers, including subsidized-housing KPR debtors) bear the loss. Developers do the selling; notaries authenticate PPJBs but have no duty or means to check other notaries' deeds. Banks (BTN and other KPR lenders) finance against PPJB-stage collateral.

searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient & Who Rejects the Existing Anchor

searchIndex.title: Coalition Loyalty Point Liabilities (axis 3)
searchIndex.text: The honest answer: nobody rejects the anchor. Partners sign contracts accepting the program owner's ledger and audit rights; banks accept Garuda's ledger; merchants accept GPI's. The disputes that do occur (Aimia/Air Canada) are about economics and control, and no tamper-evident ledger changes them.

searchIndex.text: KILLED (#2, #3, #4). Phase 1's database-is-enough verdict on retail loyalty extends to coalitions: the coalition operator is the accepted trust anchor, by contract.

searchIndex.text: Sistem Resi Gudang (SRG) lets farmers and traders deposit commodities (paddy, rice, corn, coffee, pepper, seaweed, salt, tin, others) in an approved warehouse and receive a resi gudang — a document of title that can be sold or pledged to a bank for credit. searchIndex.title: Warehouse Receipts (Sistem Resi Gudang) — Receipt Integrity (Axis 2A)
searchIndex.text: Farmers, cooperatives, and traders deposit goods and pay storage plus registration fees; they are the intended beneficiaries but have minimal ability to pay. Warehouse operators do issuance; LPK does quality attestation; KBI operates the registry and collects registration fees; banks (BRI, BJB, regi

searchIndex.text: - Warehouse operator failure: the documented legal failure mode is operator default/bankruptcy leaving receipt holders and lien holders exposed — analyzed in Indonesian legal literature on receipt-holder protection when the pengelola gudang goes bankrupt (ResearchGate/UNES law journal, 2022). searchIndex.text: - Bank hesitancy: legal studies document that banks remain reluctant SRG lenders due to commodity price risk, execution difficulty on collateral, and operator quality — not due to inability to verify receipts (Jurnal Hukum Samudra Keadilan, 2023).

searchIndex.title: Credential-to-Person Binding at Point of Hire/Care

searchIndex.title: Credential-to-Person Binding at Point of Hire/Care

searchIndex.title: Credential-to-Person Binding at Point of Hire/Care
searchIndex.text: - Data position 4 — Dukcapil-backed face-match is a commodity API resellable by any competitor (Verihubs, VIDA, Privy all offer it); a cross-hospital impostor-registry would accrue value but is unbuilt.

searchIndex.title: Credential-to-Person Binding at Point of Hire/Care
searchIndex.text: - Absorption distance 5 — plausible absorber (MedTrack/SINNAKES bolt-on) exists but no cited roadmap.

searchIndex.title: Credential-to-Person Binding at Point of Hire/Care
searchIndex.text: - Competition 6 — no dedicated identity-binding-for-hiring vendor found despite EN+ID search; adjacent generic-eKYC and generic-background-check players exist but none combine the two functions.

searchIndex.title: Credential-to-Person Binding at Point of Hire/Care
searchIndex.text: - Moat 5 — integration lock-in today; a reusable cross-hospital "verified-once" credential passport would create real network effects if built.

searchIndex.text: ## Kill Tests

searchIndex.title: Cross-Registry Credential Verification Platform
searchIndex.text: - **K1 Data access — PASS.** All five source registries are free, public, queryable without cooperation from the person being checked. Risk noted, not fatal: portals are built for single lookups (likely CAPTCHA-gated), no official bulk API exists, so scraping-at-scale carries ToS/legal-access risk t

Identity-*binding* fraud (Susanto) is a different, adjacent problem (does the holder match the person in front of you) that a registry-truth product does not so

searchIndex.title: Cross-Registry Credential Verification Platform

Each registry keeps digitizing independently (SATUSEHAT SDMK, SIVIL, SIKI), which is per-registry hardening, not cross-registry aggregation — the product's exact function.

searchIndex.title: Cross-Registry Credential Verification Platform
searchIndex.text: - **K4 Bootstrap Bar — PASS (weak-to-moderate evidence).** Plausible named segments and a proven-to-exist commercial-wrapper model (cekskk.com), but no first-party Indonesian ACV disclosed for this exact product shape.

searchIndex.title: Cross-Registry Credential Verification Platform

searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of mid-2026)

searchIndex.title: eKYC Deepfake Injection Defense
searchIndex.text: This is the most competitively contested of the three candidates. Global liveness/IDV vendors are actively racing into injection-attack defense:

searchIndex.title: eKYC Deepfake Injection Defense
searchIndex.text: - **iProov**: published research (Dec 2025) demonstrating face-swap/virtual-camera bypass of liveness on financial apps, and achieved **CEN 18099 "High" Level 2** injection-attack certification from Ingenium (Nov 2025) — the first standard of its kind for this attack class.

searchIndex.title: eKYC Deepfake Injection Defense
searchIndex.text: - **Paravision**: achieved PAD Level 3 in an Ingenium evaluation (Aug 2025).

searchIndex.title: eKYC Deepfake Injection Defense
searchIndex.text: - **Innovatrics**: as of the 2026 sourced article, does **not yet** hold formal injection-attack certification — holds Substantial-level presentation-attack (not injection-attack) certification from CLR Labs (valid 2026-2028) and is "working toward" injection-level certification, though independent

searchIndex.title: eKYC Deepfake Injection Defense
searchIndex.text: - Sumsub and Mitek are referenced in general industry coverage as building injection detection into 2025-era releases, but this was not independently verified via primary source and should be treated as **weakly sourced**.

searchIndex.title: eKYC Deepfake Injection Defense
searchIndex.text: - No direct evidence was found confirming which vendor(s) Indonesian banks currently use for liveness, or that any Indonesian-market vendor (VIDA, PrivyID, Verihubs) shipped dedicated injection detection as of mid-2026.

searchIndex.title: eKYC Deepfake Injection Defense
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Tests

searchIndex.title: eKYC Deepfake Injection Defense
searchIndex.text: - **K1 (Data access): PASS.** The bank/lender already owns the entire onboarding video/device pipeline; detection relies on device, driver, and stream-integrity signals the customer already possesses, not cooperation from the fraudulent applicant.

searchIndex.title: eKYC Deepfake Injection Defense
searchIndex.text: - **K2 (Oracle bound): PASS.** Injection is technically inferable from camera-driver signature verification, sensor-consistency checks, and dynamic challenge-response (e.g., iProov's Flashmark-style approach) — a demonstrated technical approach, not a fabricated-at-source physical truth.

searchIndex.title: eKYC Deepfake Injection Defense
searchIndex.text: - **K3 (Absorption): PASS, with the strongest residual risk of the three candidates.** Global incumbent liveness vendors (iProov, Paravision) shipped certified injection-attack defenses within the past 12 months (Aug-Nov 2025) — real, dated evidence of "incumbent already entering the exact function.

searchIndex.title: eKYC Deepfake Injection Defense
searchIndex.text: - **K4 (Bootstrap bar): PASS, weak evidence.** Single-sided market (no cold-start problem, unlike the receivables candidate) with a plausible self-serve beachhead in P2P/multifinance lenders, but ACV lacks a real Indonesian comparable and bank-tier customers likely require enterprise-style security

searchIndex.text: **Survives: YES**, but this is the closest call of the three and carries the highest competitive/absorption risk.

searchIndex.text: A PKP (VAT-registered) buyer in Indonesia claims input-VAT credit against a "faktur pajak" it receives from a supplier. (1) DJP's Coretax system, mandatory since 1 Jan 2025, lets a buyer scan a QR code or check its dashboard to confirm an invoice is "sah" (exists, correctly formatted, active NPWP) — but this only confirms the document is real in DJP's ledger, not

searchIndex.title: Fictitious Tax-Invoice (Faktur) Detection & Counterparty Screening
