searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Coffee & Cocoa Provenance (coffee-cocoa)
searchIndex.text: Work: ~1.8 million coffee-farming households (unverified), collectors, cooperatives (e.g., Gayo cooperatives under MPKG for GI), exporters, grinders (Barry Callebaut, Cargill, ofi, JB Cocoa), specialty importers and roasters. Pays: exporters and grinders fund compliance; EU/US roasters pay origin pr

searchIndex.title: Coffee & Cocoa Provenance (coffee-cocoa)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Coffee & Cocoa Provenance (coffee-cocoa)
searchIndex.text: - Kopi luwak adulteration: an academic test reported ~41% of kopi luwak sold in the US market was adulterated or blended (reported by specialtycoffee.id, citing prior research; primary study not independently verified here — weak source). Gayo arabica is routinely passed off as luwak.

searchIndex.title: Coffee & Cocoa Provenance (coffee-cocoa)
searchIndex.text: - Gayo counterfeiting: Indonesian consumer press documents persistent fake/oplosan "Gayo" in domestic and export channels (IDN Times; Kompas, 2016–2024); no authority publishes loss figures — economic scale (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Coffee & Cocoa Provenance (coffee-cocoa)
searchIndex.text: - EUDR panic-buying: anticipation of the original December 2025 deadline triggered heavy front-loading of EU shipments — over 1.4 million bags moved through Belgium and Germany in early 2025 (USDA FAS, 2025) — evidence that origin-compliance uncertainty, not demand, is moving trade.

searchIndex.title: Coffee & Cocoa Provenance (coffee-cocoa)
searchIndex.text: - Farmer-level data fabrication is the sector's acknowledged weak point: polygons drawn from office desks, borrowed STDB-equivalents, and collector-level mixing mean documents describe farms, not lots. (Pattern documented across EUDR-readiness reporting; AgTech Navigator, August 2025.)

searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Coffee & Cocoa Provenance (coffee-cocoa)
searchIndex.text: - Exposure: over 30% of Indonesia's coffee export value is linked to Europe (indonesia-coffee.com, 2025 — secondary, weak); coffee exports earned $1.64 billion in 2024 (Indonesia Investments). Losing EU access is a >$500M/yr revenue risk (derived, unverified).

searchIndex.title: Coffee & Cocoa Provenance (coffee-cocoa)
searchIndex.text: - Specialty fraud losses: no named Indonesian figure exists — (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Coffee & Cocoa Provenance (coffee-cocoa)
searchIndex.text: - Compliance cost per farmer polygon/registration: (unverified); donor-funded programs absorb most of it today.

Koltiva runs KoltiTrace across cocoa and coffee with corporat

searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Coffee & Cocoa Provenance (coffee-cocoa)
searchIndex.text: Every platform depends on self-reported or enumerator-collected farm data; none can prove that a given bag came from the polygon attached to it once collectors blend lots — the mass-balance gap. GI enforcement (Gayo) has paperwork but no lot-level verification, so premiums leak to counterfeiters. Ye

searchIndex.text: Multi-org chain with adversarial premium incentives and foreign verifiers looks chain-shaped, but accepted trusted intermediaries already exist (certifiers, Enveritas, state surveyor, Koltiva), and the EU accepts centrally filed DDS. The failure mode is data capture and physical mixing, which no led

searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.text: # Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: Pharma: manufacturer or importer → CDOB-certified distributor (PBF) → hospital/pharmacy/puskesmas. BPOM's CDOB (Good Distribution Practice) rules require validated cold rooms, calibrated monitoring, and — for cold-chain products such as vaccines — checking transit temperature records and Vaccine Via

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: Work: cold storage operators, reefer fleets (MGM Bosco and peers), PBFs, food processors, fisheries, importers. Pays: brand owners and PBFs pay for compliant logistics; insurers pay spoilage claims; consumers pay via waste priced into food. Audits: BPOM (pharma), buyers' QA teams, insurers' surveyor

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents, cited)

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - The structural failure: temperature logs are custodial and self-reported. Each party runs its own logger; gaps, resets, or transcription happen at precisely the handoffs where liability transfers. BPOM treats failure to document storage temperature as a serious violation (Farmasetika, 2026), which

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - Sanctions exist and are used: BPOM Reg 20/2025 codifies suspension and electronic revocation of CDOB certificates for critical findings (BPK regulation database, 2025). Named public enforcement cases tied specifically to falsified temperature logs: none found in search (unverified — disputes appea

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - Waste scale: Bappenas' FLW study (2021) put Indonesian food loss and waste at 23–48 million tonnes/year, an economic loss of Rp213–551 trillion/year (4–5% of GDP); loss (pre-retail, cold-chain-addressable) was ~45% of the total by 2019.

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - Global reference: claims that up to 50% of vaccines are wasted globally from cold-chain breaks circulate in vendor literature (unverified; WHO-derived figure, contested methodology).

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - Food loss economic cost: Rp213–551 trillion/yr (Bappenas, 2021) — only a fraction is attributable to cold-chain trust rather than absent cold-chain capacity (attribution unverified).

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - Market context: Indonesia cold chain market ~USD 3.0B in 2024 growing ~9.5% CAGR to 2030 (MarkNtel, 2025); a rival estimate says USD 8.4B in 2026 (MarkWide, 2026) — definitions differ, treat both as vendor estimates.

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - Fisheries: with proper cold chain, losses reportedly fall to 5–8% (Daxtro vendor blog, 2025 — unverified).

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - Pharma dispute/claims cost in Indonesia: no named figure found (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07, named)

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - Indonesian operators: Coldspace (integrated cold chain, $3.8M seed May 2023 from Intudo/ASSA/Triputra; ~3,000t own capacity plus 30,000t marketplace at raise), MGM Bosco (merged transport+storage incumbent, 100+ cities), Deliveree and Waresix touch reefer freight marginally.

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - Monitoring vendors (global, present via distributors): Sensitech, Berlinger, Elpro, Controlant-style real-time IoT loggers; local integrators retrofit reefers with cellular sensors (market reports, 2025-26). One market report claims IoT loggers with "blockchain-anchored data integrity" feeding BPO

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - Government: BPOM CDOB certification + inspection regime; Kemenkes cold-chain infrastructure program for immunization (Kemenkes, 2023).

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: - No funded Indonesian startup focused on neutral cross-party temperature evidence was found after search — but the adjacent ops/monitoring space is occupied.

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: Monitoring hardware answers "what was the temperature" but not "whose record governs when parties disagree." In practice the shipper's logger, the carrier's telematics, and the warehouse's WMS each tell their own story, and insurers arbitrate with discretionary haircuts. CDOB compels documentation b

searchIndex.title: Cold Chain — Food & Pharma (cold-chain)
searchIndex.text: The gap has a proven non-blockchain answer: a third-party monitoring vendor whose single feed is contractually accepted by shipper, carrier, and insurer — the Controlant model that won global pharma logistics — is PostgreSQL under a trusted operator. Multi-org, yes; but an accepted neutral intermedi

searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED

searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain? YES. 2. PostgreSQL under one trusted operator? YES — neutral-vendor telemetry accepted by contract solves it (fails). 3. searchIndex.text: - Moat 5 — sensor fleet plus insurer/BPOM acceptance is integration lock-in, not a protocol position.

searchIndex.text: # Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: Researched 2026-07-29. Phase 1 scan, pre-committed rubric.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: Indonesian construction payments run on progress billing (termin). A typical private contract pays in tranches — e.g., after 30%, 70%, and 100% completion — while government contracts pay monthly against a Monthly Certificate (Ajaib, 2021; tekniksipil.id). Each payment requires a chain of paper appr

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: Subcontractors sit at the end of the chain. "Pay-when-paid" and "pay-when-certified" clauses are legally enforceable in Indonesia and are standard practice, so a subcontractor is paid only after the main contractor is paid, regardless of its own performance (ASCE Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Owners: government (PUPR, local governments via LPSE), SOEs, private developers — pay main contractors.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Main contractors: state (Waskita Karya, WIKA, PP, Adhi Karya) and private — pay hundreds of subcontractors and suppliers ("vendors").

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Subcontractors/vendors: bear the cash-flow risk; finance work from their own balance sheets or expensive credit.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Supervising consultants (MK/konsultan pengawas) certify progress; BPK/BPKP audit state projects; LPJK/PUPR police licensing; BANI and commercial courts (PKPU) handle disputes; banks provide working capital and supply-chain financing.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Waskita Karya accumulated vendor (subcontractor/supplier) arrears of Rp2.1 trillion due through 2024; ~82% has been paid, leaving Rp383 billion outstanding (Liputan6, 2025; Bloomberg Technoz, 2023 — Waskita held Rp4.6T cash it could not release to vendors because restructuring covenants required c

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Vendor PT Megah Bangun Baja Semesta filed a PKPU (suspension-of-payments) petition against Waskita, accepted February 2023 (CNBC Indonesia, 2023).

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Waskita defaulted on Rp1.36 trillion of bond principal and interest (IDNFinancials, 2023). Shares remain suspended on IDX as of mid-2026; total liabilities cut from ~Rp84T (2023) to Rp67.1T, with Rp722 billion of non-guaranteed bonds still to restructure before September 2026 (Indonesia Business P

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - WIKA carries Rp29 trillion of interest-bearing debt (Rp19T bank, Rp10T bonds/sukuk) (IDX Channel, 2025). Bondholders approved restructuring of 27 bond and sukuk series in April 2026; completion targeted H2 2026 (Bisnis.com, May 2026).

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Forged SBU business certificates are common enough that LPJK now works with police on criminal enforcement; using fake/expired SBU carries fines up to Rp1 billion under UU 2/2017 (SmartLegal.id, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Rp2.1 trillion vendor arrears at one contractor alone (Waskita; Bloomberg Technoz/Liputan6, 2023–2025).

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Globally, sums in dispute on construction claims average 33.4% of contract budgets (HKA CRUX 8th Annual Report, 2025 — global figure, no Indonesia-specific breakdown published).

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Late payment demonstrably degrades subcontractor financial health and project productivity (Jurnal Konstruksia UMJ; qualitative).

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Indonesia construction market: USD 329.4 billion output in 2026 (Mordor Intelligence, 2026). Aggregate Indonesia-specific dispute/delay cost: (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Doxa Connex (Singapore fintech): procure-to-pay for construction with a Subcon module handling progress claims, payment certificates, variation orders; DBS partnership for automated supplier payments; 1,000+ construction companies in ecosystem; piloting in Indonesia via National Hospital Surabaya

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Gravel (Indonesia, US$14M from NEA et al., 2023): construction workforce/materials marketplace, 12,000+ projects — adjacent, not payment certification (Katadata, 2023).

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Government systems: LPSE e-procurement, LPJK/SIMPK SBU verification portals.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Global: Oracle Textura, Procore, GCPay — payment-application platforms; no material Indonesian deployment surfaced in searches.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Banks: supply-chain financing/invoice financing against contractor receivables; Waskita/WIKA Master Restructuring Agreements govern SOE payment waterfalls.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: The approval chain (opname → berita acara → certificate → invoice) is still bilateral paper; subcontractors cannot cheaply prove a certified receivable to a financier, and pay-when-paid remains legal. But the deepest documented failure is solvency, not record integrity: Waskita's vendors held valid,

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: A shared tamper-evident ledger of progress certificates would help subcontractor financing. However, banks are an accepted trusted intermediary in this chain — Doxa+DBS already operate exactly this model on conventional infrastructure. Tamper-evidence does not unlock payment when the payer is insolv

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain? YES (passes).

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 2. Would PostgreSQL under a trusted operator solve it? YES — a bank- or platform-operated payment-certification and SCF system (Doxa Connex model) is accepted by all parties. FAILS.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 3. Could an incumbent ship it in 6 months? Plausibly — Doxa already ships the Subcon workflow regionally and is entering Indonesia. FAILS.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone value? Yes in principle (Doxa's existence proves it), but 2 and 3 already kill the blockchain venture.

searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.text: - Severity 7 — recurring vendor losses, PKPU filings, dedicated restructuring apparatus; documented multi-trillion-rupiah arrears.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Market 6 — USD 329B output (Mordor, 2026) is verified, but capturable software/fintech TAM is (unverified); between $250M–1B plausible.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 5 — budget owners exist (owners, banks) but the natural buyers (main contractors) are financially distressed.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 5 — multi-org, but banks/platforms are accepted trusted intermediaries (anchor case).

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 5 — restructurings conclude 2026, pressure real, but no regulatory deadline forcing new payment infrastructure.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 5 — several attempts (Doxa regional, Gravel adjacent, global vendors), none dominant in Indonesia.

searchIndex.title: Construction — Payments & Approvals (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 5 — integration lock-in achievable; workflows copyable.

searchIndex.text: # Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Roughly 4–5 million Pekerja Migran Indonesia (PMI) — count varies by source, many undocumented (unverified) — remit from Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Singapore, Korea, Japan. Sending workflow today: worker is placed via a P3MI placement agency (contract, placement-cost schedule, KP2MI

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Workers pay fees and FX margin; families bear delays. Operators (banks, MTOs, fintechs) pay licensing and compliance. BI regulates payments; OJK regulates crypto-assets and consumer protection; KP2MI/BP2MI protects workers; PPATK monitors AML. P3MI agencies control the placement funnel and are also

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: This corridor's trust failures sit mostly **upstream of the money rail**: overcharging of placement fees and non-procedural migration exposing workers to fraud and trafficking are the persistent, government-acknowledged problems (Kemenko PM consultation, Antara, 2025; KP2MI "Migran Aman" campaign, 2

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Volume: PMI remittances Rp 253.3 trillion (~USD 15.8B) in 2024 (KP2MI via Kompas, April 2025); 2025 up ~14% to roughly Rp 288 trillion (Minister of P2MI via Antara, 2025/2026); BI put the PMI contribution at USD 14.22B for the prior period (BI via CNBC Indonesia, May 2024). Remittances ≈1.2% of GD

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Price: global average remittance cost 6.49% (World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide Issue 53, March 2025); Malaysia→Indonesia via Western Union 3.24% total cost as of October 2025 (World Bank RPW corridor data, 2025). At a blended 3–5% on ~USD 16B, workers pay roughly USD 0.5–0.8B/year in fees and

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Overcharging/placement-fee losses: no verified aggregate (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **State infrastructure (the big one)**: BI joined the BIS **Project Nexus**; Nexus Global Payments incorporated in Singapore by BNM, BSP, MAS, BOT, RBI with BI as special observer; BI plans BI-FAST linkage with domestic settlement kept onshore; go-live targeted 2026–2027 (Antara, 2025; The Asian B

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Fintech**: Wise, Topremit (Medan-based BI-licensed remitter), Flip Globe — active Indonesian corridors (operational status widely reported; sites blocked verification 2026-07, license details unverified); incumbent MTOs Western Union/MoneyGram; bank remittance subsidiaries.

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Crypto rails**: stablecoin settlement is used by some regional B2B providers, but industry is still lobbying BI for legal recognition of stablecoins for payments (Coinpedia, 2025); using them consumer-facing in Indonesia is prohibited.

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Costs above the UN 3% SDG target persist on Gulf corridors, and non-procedural workers remain locked out of formal rails. But the deficit is being closed by exactly the actor best placed to close it: central banks interlinking instant-payment systems multilaterally. What remains unsolved — worker le

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: The trust problem between sending PSP, receiving PSP, and regulators is being solved by an accepted neutral intermediary (Nexus Global Payments, owned by the central banks themselves). BI explicitly requires settlement to remain in domestic systems. A blockchain rail would have to route around BI in

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain? YES (fees, exclusion).

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under one trusted operator? YES — Nexus is literally a trusted multilateral operator interlinking existing ledgers; anchors say chain=5 territory at best. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 3. Incumbent ships in six months? Not in six months, but central banks and Wise/Topremit are already shipping the roadmap; a startup adds no wedge. Effectively FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone value? Fee pool exists (~USD 0.5B+), but margin is compressing by policy design, and the licensable path forbids the blockchain variant.

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Severity 5 — measurable cost (3–6% of transfers) with working workarounds; upstream abuses are severe but out of scope for a settlement product.

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Market 7 — fee pool on ~USD 16B verified flows sits in the USD 250M–1B band.

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - WTP 3 — payers are price-sensitive migrant workers; no institutional budget owner for a new rail.

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Chain 5 — multi-org, but accepted trusted intermediaries exist and are strengthening (Nexus, QRIS x-border).

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 5 — growing policy momentum, no deadline forcing private action.

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Competition 3 — Wise, MTOs, licensed local fintechs, and state infrastructure all funded and moving.

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Moat 3 — a new entrant's only moat would be licenses incumbents already hold.

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Weighted: 4.7**

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.title: Migrant Remittances & Settlement — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Already killed: kill-test 2 fails, BI's crypto-payment prohibition forecloses the blockchain variant outright, and Nexus/QRIS compress the margin the business would need. Revisit only if Nexus stalls past 2028 AND BI licenses stablecoin settlement — neither indicated as of July 2026.

searchIndex.text: # Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: Identity in Indonesia anchors on Dukcapil's population register (NIK, e-KTP, biometric records). Verification today: a relying party (bank, fintech, telco) collects KTP photo + selfie, runs OCR and face-match against Dukcapil through a licensed access agreement or an e-KYC vendor, then binds the ide

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: Dukcapil owns the root registry; Komdigi licenses PSrE; OJK and BI impose KYC obligations that force banks, multifinance, fintech lenders, and crypto exchanges to pay per-verification and per-signature fees — these regulated entities are the paying customers and already pay incumbents. Employers and

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents, cited)

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Deepfake/biometric spoofing: fintech losses tied to deepfake cases exceed US$138.5 million, on a 1,550% surge in AI-driven fraud 2022–2024, much of it biometric spoofing during loan applications (VIDA fraud report via vida.id, 2024/2025).

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Account takeover: 97% of Indonesian businesses faced account-takeover attempts in 2024; digital document forgeries up 244% YoY (VIDA, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Bulk identity data for sale: alleged 337 million Dukcapil records offered by a hacker (Kumparan, 2023); 279 million records incident (2021); 6 million NPWP records offered for ~Rp150 million (Bjorka post, Tempo, Sept 2024). Cheap stolen NIK/KK data feeds synthetic-identity loan fraud.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Credential forgery: Udinus became the first Indonesian campus issuing 100% blockchain-based diplomas explicitly to fight ijazah forgery (Udinus, Feb 2026) — indicating both the problem and that issuers are already acting.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - US$138.5M+ deepfake-linked fintech losses (VIDA, 2025) — vendor-published figure, treat as directional.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Per-incident and aggregate national identity-fraud losses: (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Compliance spend: every OJK-regulated onboarding requires paid e-KYC; total market value (unverified, but Privy alone processed 40M+ signatures/year at Series C — Businesswire, 2022).

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07, named)

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - State: Dukcapil IKD — 20.5 million active users by July 2026 against a 30% population target (Dirjen Dukcapil via lpc-online, July 2026; weak outlet, figure directionally consistent with Kemendagri statements); INA Digital/INApas in limited release.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Privy: US$48M Series C led by KKR (Businesswire, Nov 2022); 30M verified users then, >52M by Oct 2024 (Hukumonline, 2024), claims of 71M users and 200k organizations by May 2026 (pojokpapua, 2026 — unverified).

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - VIDA: licensed PSrE, aggressive deepfake-detection product line and fraud research.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Peruri: state-owned PSrE and operator of INA Digital.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - e-KYC/biometrics vendors: Verihubs, Nodeflux, ASLI RI (competitive state as of 2026-07 not re-verified this session).

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Global: Jumio, Sumsub, iProov sell into the region; W3C VC tooling (open source) freely available.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: Real gaps exist: breached static data means possession of NIK+selfie no longer proves personhood; credentials are not machine-verifiable across issuers; IKD and INApas overlap confusingly. But every gap sits on territory already claimed: the state owns the root registry and is building the wallet; l

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: Multi-org, yes — but every relying party already accepts trusted intermediaries: Dukcapil as identity root and PSrE as certifiers. W3C VC works fine with plain PKI; a chain adds nothing the Komdigi trust list doesn't provide. Issuer-independent verification (the one honest chain argument, e.g., dipl

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain: YES. 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator just as good: YES — fails. Dukcapil + licensed PSrE are exactly that, and are accepted by regulators and courts. 3. Incumbent ships it in 6 months: YES — fails. Privy or VIDA can add VC issuance/verification atop exi

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 7 — recurring, rising fraud losses with dedicated fraud teams at every lender (VIDA 2025), but not existential for the payers.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Market 6 — mandated e-KYC/signature spend across all OJK-regulated onboarding plausibly $250M+; verified basis thin, so scored below 7.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 8 — mandated compliance spend; buyers demonstrably pay incumbents today.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 4 — accepted trusted intermediaries exist at both root (Dukcapil) and certification (PSrE) layers.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 6 — deepfake surge and INApas rollout create pressure, but no deadline forcing a new vendor.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 3 — funded incumbents with traction (Privy $48M+, VIDA, Peruri) plus the state itself.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 4 — PSrE licensing is a barrier that protects incumbents, not entrants; integrations lock in the installed base.

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: Weighted: 5.7

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.title: Digital Identity & Verifiable Credentials (digital-identity)
searchIndex.text: Already killed: incumbent capture. The only survivable wedge would be issuer-independent credential provenance for cross-border verification (workers, diplomas) — narrow, low WTP, and attackable by incumbents the moment it shows revenue.

searchIndex.text: # Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: A typical inter-city FTL shipment: shipper issues a delivery order (DO) to a 3PL or forwarder; the job is frequently re-brokered one or two layers down to a vendor fleet or individual truck owner. The driver carries a paper surat jalan (delivery note) listing cargo, route and consignee; at destinati

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: Work: drivers, truck-owner SMEs (often 1–10 units), vendor fleets, brokers/forwarders, 3PLs. Pays: cargo owners (FMCG, manufacturing, commodities) pay freight; carriers absorb fraud, theft and claim deductions; financiers (invoice financing) absorb document risk. Audits: shippers' logistics and AP d

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents, cited)

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - Driver cargo embezzlement (penggelapan muatan) is routine and criminal-court documented: three expedition drivers in Surabaya diverted portions of loads en route, company loss Rp108 million (Kompas, May 2026); a driver contracted to PT Global Link Logistic charged with embezzling cargo worth nearl

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - Fictitious-load scams: drivers lured with fake cargo orders (RRI, 2025-26).

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - Fuel fraud: "kencing solar" — tank-truck drivers siphoning hundreds of litres per trip — described in a DPR/parliamentary discussion (Wartajatim, November 2025). At national scale, the 2025 Pertamina case alleged adulteration of subsidised fuel with prosecutors' loss estimate of Rp968.5 trillion (

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - Truck hijacking/begal on expedition routes, packages worth hundreds of millions of rupiah taken (Berita Cianjur, 2025-26).

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - Logistics cost to GDP: Bappenas puts it at 14.29% (2023, new methodology), down from 23.8% (2018, old methodology) — the two are not comparable; one DPR brief still cites ~23.27% for 2023 under the broader definition (DPR Info Singkat, October 2025). Any pitch using "24% of GDP" is stale.

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - World Bank LPI 2023: Indonesia ranked 61 of 139, down from 46 (2018).

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - Cargo crime: only case-level figures exist (Rp108M–Rp360M per incident, 2026 court/police reports); no national aggregate found (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - POD-driven working-capital drag: no named study found (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07, named)

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - McEasy (Surabaya): telematics + TMS SaaS, ~$19M raised, Series A+ led by Granite Asia closed December 2024 (Tracxn/SaaS News) — alive and funded.

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - Kargo Technologies: marketplace, Series B July 2024, pivoting into EV fleet (500 e-trucks planned 2025; DealStreetAsia) — alive.

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - Deliveree: ~$110M raised, GTV >$100M claimed 2024 (Techloy/Tracxn) — alive, regional.

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - Waresix: $179M raised, still listed operating (Tracxn, May 2026). Logisly: operating, profitability-focused (LinkedIn/company posts, 2024). Andalin: operating, ~69 employees (PitchBook, 2026).

searchIndex.title: Domestic Freight & Trucking (domestic-logistics)
searchIndex.text: - All major platforms already ship e-POD (photo + geotag + digital signature) inside their apps. Global visibility vendors (project44, FourKites) have thin Indonesian presence (unverified).

searchIndex.text: # E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Counterfeit goods circulate at scale on Indonesian marketplaces (Shopee, Tokopedia/ShopTokopedia, Bukalapak, Lazada, TikTok Shop live commerce). A brand that wants a fake removed today follows this chain: (1) hold a registered trademark at DJKI (Direktorat Jenderal Kekayaan Intelektual) — registrati

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Work is done by brand-protection teams at consumer brands (cosmetics, fashion, pharma, auto parts), their law firms (Rouse, AFFA), and SaaS vendors. Brands pay. Marketplaces bear moderation cost and reputational/USTR exposure. DJKI and Bea Cukai audit and enforce; MIAP (Masyarakat Indonesia Anti Pem

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - USTR 2024 Notorious Markets Review again lists Shopee and Bukalapak for "high volumes of counterfeit products" and weak repeat-offender penalties; Tokopedia was delisted after removing 80M+ infringing listings and sanctioning 43,000+ sellers in 2023 (USTR via Magpie IQ / Conventus Law, 2024).

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Indonesia has sat on the USTR Priority Watch List for IP for 16 consecutive years (USTR, 2025).

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - DJKI's December 2025 evidence-destruction event cited seized counterfeit goods with potential losses of Rp 3.07 billion in that batch alone (Tempo, 2025).

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Seller evasion is systematic: account cycling after takedowns, image reuse, 40–70% price undercutting (Magpie IQ, 2026).

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Economy-wide counterfeiting cost Rp 291 trillion, Rp 967 billion in lost tax, and 2M+ lost jobs per the MIAP–IEALP UPH study of 2020 (published 2021; MIAP runs it five-yearly) — the canonical figure, dated, and economy-wide rather than e-commerce-specific.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - 5–10% of Indonesian marketplace transactions estimated fraudulent (Cube Asia, 2025).

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Indonesia e-commerce GMV exceeded USD 75B in 2024 (Magpie IQ citing industry data, 2025) — even 5% counterfeit share implies multi-billion-dollar flows (derived, unverified).

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Brand-side spend on monitoring subscriptions, test purchases, and legal fees: no Indonesia-specific aggregate found (unverified).

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Marketplace-native**: Tokopedia IP Protection portal, Shopee IPR flow, TikTok Shop "zero tolerance" policy with automated pre-listing detection.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Government**: DJKI trademark registry and PPNS enforcement; DJKI anti-counterfeiting mall certification program (2025); Bea Cukai IP recordation; DJKI–IDEA marketplace MoU track.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Global SaaS**: Red Points, Corsearch (Zeal), MarqVision (publishes Tokopedia takedown guides), BrandShield, Podqi — all cover Indonesian platforms.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Indonesia-focused**: Magpie IQ "Owl" (monitors six Indonesian platforms, transaction-signal detection); Shieldtag (Jakarta, hologram + QR + PIN authentication, used by Azarine, Zoya); SeQure (copy-proof QR); CekKeaslian. BPOM pharma serialization (2D barcode track-and-trace) is mandated complian

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Detection-takedown is a treadmill: enforcement is per-listing while sellers respawn, and live commerce evades listing-based monitoring entirely. Cross-platform repeat-offender identity is not shared between marketplaces, so a banned Shopee seller reopens on TikTok Shop. Physical authentication (Shie

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Provenance-on-chain does not bind a token to a physical good any better than a QR code bound to a Postgres row; the counterfeiter copies the code either way. Marketplace, brand, and regulator already accept trusted intermediaries (DJKI registry, marketplace portals). A shared repeat-offender blackli

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain? YES (physical counterfeiting).

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 2. Would PostgreSQL under one trusted operator solve it? YES — brand-protection SaaS and serialization registries are exactly that, and they function. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 3. Could an incumbent ship it in six months? YES — marketplaces already run IP portals; Red Points/MarqVision already cover Indonesia. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone value? Exists, but already captured by funded incumbents.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Severity 7 — recurring losses, USTR/regulatory exposure, dedicated brand-protection staff exist.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Market 5 — Indonesian brand-protection spend plausibly USD 50–250M; economy-wide damage is large but not addressable revenue.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - WTP 7 — brands already pay Red Points/Corsearch/law firms for an imperfect alternative.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Chain 3 — single-org detection; database plus QR suffices.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 5 — annual USTR pressure, no hard deadline.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Competition 3 — funded incumbents with traction, global and local.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Moat 3 — detection features are copyable; no protocol position available.

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Weighted: 5.0**

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.title: E-commerce Counterfeits & Brand Protection — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Already killed: kill-test questions 2 and 3 fail, and competition is saturated. The only defensible variant — a cross-marketplace seller-identity blacklist — belongs to IDEA/Komdigi or the platforms themselves, not a startup.

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: Issuance: an accredited university reports each graduate to PDDikti (the national higher-education database), obtains a national diploma number via PISN, and prints the ijazah. Since Permendikbudristek 58/2024, primary and secondary schools issue e-ijazah with certified electronic signatures startin

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: Universities and LLDIKTI issue and correct records; Kemendiktisaintek operates PDDikti/SIVIL/PISN free of charge. Employers and government recruiters (CPNS/PPPK) bear verification effort and pay screening firms such as Integrity Indonesia (PBSA-accredited) and Veremark when stakes are high. Graduate

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - May 2023: Kemendikbudristek revoked operating licenses of 23 private universities for fictitious instruction, diploma selling (jual beli ijazah), and KIP-K scholarship abuse, from 52 public complaints; 29 more campuses were under review (CNN Indonesia; Kompas, 2023).

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - March–December 2025: the Jokowi ijazah affair — allegations that the ex-president's UGM diploma was fake escalated into a national legal saga; Bareskrim declared the diploma genuine, and Polda Metro Jaya named 8 suspects including Roy Suryo for defamation and data manipulation (Antara; Kompas, 202

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - Recurring false negatives: legitimate alumni report diploma numbers missing from SIVIL due to campus reporting lapses (Universitas Trunojoyo alumni complaints, 2023), forcing manual remediation.

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: No credible aggregate rupiah figure for diploma fraud exists (unverified). Verified proxies: 23 campuses closed in one 2023 enforcement wave (Kemendikbudristek, 2023); only 15% of universities had adopted digital diplomas as of 2025 (Kemendikbudristek figure reported by Blockchain Media Indonesia, 2

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - Government: PDDikti + SIVIL + PISN (free public lookup); e-ijazah with certified digital signature for schools from 2025 (Permendikbudristek 58/2024); SatuDikti app.

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - State incumbent moving into blockchain: Peruri Digital Security (PDS) announced a blockchain digital-ijazah collaboration with Kemendikdasmen on 23 June 2025 (PDS, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - Campus-led: Universitas Dian Nuswantoro (Udinus) launched Indonesia's first "100% blockchain" diplomas on 7 February 2026 with Sealbound UAE, Indonesia Blockchain Center, and Dubai Blockchain Center (Udinus; Detik, 2026).

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - Private: background-check firms (Integrity Indonesia, T2 Intelligence, Veremark); certified e-signature providers (PSrE: Peruri, Privy, VIDA); campus SIS vendors (SEVIMA) that already integrate PDDikti reporting.

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: The real gaps are coverage and data hygiene, not absence of a trust anchor: pre-2002 graduates, closed campuses, non-degree certificates, and unreported cohorts fall outside SIVIL; false negatives punish honest graduates. None of this is fixed by adding a second ledger — it requires backfilling reco

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: Multiple parties exist (campuses, employers, state), but all parties already accept a single trusted intermediary: PDDikti/SIVIL. A PostgreSQL registry under Kemendiktisaintek is literally the incumbent architecture, and its failures are data-completeness failures. Blockchain adds nothing an authent

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: KILLED.

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem without blockchain? YES (fraud is real).

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator? YES, it solves it — SIVIL is that system; gaps are coverage, not trust. FAIL.

searchIndex.text: 3. Incumbent ships it in 6 months? YES — Peruri/Kemendikdasmen are already shipping blockchain e-ijazah; SEVIMA could add verification features. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone company value? Doubtful against a free state portal. FAIL.

searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - WTP 5 — employers already pay screening firms, but the state alternative is free, capping price.

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - Chain 3 — accepted single trusted operator (PDDikti/SIVIL) exists.

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 6 — e-ijazah regulation in force for 2025 cohorts and fresh scandal, but the deadline binds government, not customers.

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - Competition 4 — state incumbent Peruri plus Udinus/Sealbound already shipping; screening firms entrenched.

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification
searchIndex.text: - Moat 3 — a verification layer over someone else's registry is a copyable feature.

searchIndex.title: Education Credentials — Diploma & Academic Credential Verification

searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.text: Already killed: Peruri (state-owned, ministry-partnered) occupying the blockchain-ijazah slot; SIVIL closing coverage gaps by administrative backfill; free government verification making a paid product unsellable.

searchIndex.text: # Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)

searchIndex.title: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)
searchIndex.text: Hard search (English and Indonesian) found **no documented forgery, double-issuance or fraud incident involving Indonesian RECs**. The trust issues on record are structural, not criminal:

searchIndex.title: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)
searchIndex.text: - **Attribute-ownership disputes** between IPPs and PLN over who owns the environmental attribute of PPA electricity — significant enough that the I-TRACK Foundation publicly noted Indonesia's clarification of attribute ownership as a market-integrity milestone (I-TRACK Foundation, 2024).

searchIndex.title: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)
searchIndex.text: The honest finding is that the existing stack is largely *sufficient*. The single-utility structure means one counterparty (PLN) controls generation data; TIGR and Evident are accepted trusted intermediaries whose records RE100/CDP auditors already rely on. Remaining gaps — additionality, NDC double

searchIndex.title: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)
searchIndex.text: Single dominant counterparty plus internationally accepted registries. A database under a trusted operator is not the hypothetical fix — it is the current, functioning system. Tamper-evidence changes no behavior because no party disputes the registries' records.

PostgreSQL under a single trusted operator? **YES — TIGR and Evident are exactly that and are accepted by all verifiers. FAIL.** 3. searchIndex.title: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)

searchIndex.title: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)

searchIndex.title: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)

searchIndex.title: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)
searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.title: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs)
searchIndex.text: Already killed by structure: the registry layer is occupied and accepted; the utility is a monopoly; the money is small. Only a regulatory rupture (e.g., mandatory granular hourly matching, or liberalized retail wheeling creating many competing suppliers) would reopen it.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: Capture fisheries: a licensed vessel (SIPI) files an e-logbook, lands at a designated port where unloading data (bongkaran) is recorded, and the port authority issues the initial sheet that anchors the Sertifikat Hasil Tangkapan Ikan (SHTI) — the catch certificate required for EU-bound shipments und

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: Regulatory direction is softening on the US side: Executive Order 14276 (April 2025) directed Commerce to consider revising or rescinding recent SIMP expansions, after NOAA had already withdrawn its 2022 expansion rule; Congress still funded SIMP in January 2026 (CRS, 2025–2026).

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: Work: ~2.7 million fishers and fish farmers (unverified), port officers, processors/cold chains, exporters. Pays: exporters bear certificate and documentation costs; KKP funds STELINA and enforcement; US/EU importers bear filing burdens; investors and lenders pay for diligence on aquaculture venture

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: - eFishery (2025): Indonesia's aquaculture unicorn fabricated its core operational data — FTI Consulting found revenue inflated from an actual ~$157M to a claimed $752M for 9M-2024, a claimed $16M profit versus a real ~$35M loss, and ~24,000 active eFeeders versus 400,000+ claimed, with dual books s

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: - IUU fishing losses: KKP put losses at over Rp13 trillion (~$800M) for 2020–2025 (Jakarta Globe, 2025); a KKP adviser cited $23 billion in 2023 (Tempo.co, May 2023, leaning on FAO's global 26M-ton figure); older Supreme Audit Agency work suggested up to Rp300 trillion (Fair Observer, undated). The

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: - Benjina slavery case (AP investigation, 2015): trafficked crews and laundered catch moved through Indonesian ports into US supply chains — the origin story for SIMP.

searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: - IUU losses: Rp13T/2020–2025 (KKP via Jakarta Globe, 2025) to $23B/yr (KKP staffer, Tempo 2023) — figures conflict; treat all as weakly grounded.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: - eFishery: ~$1.4B in equity value destroyed (The Runway/CNBC, 2025); KWAP's RM163.4M investment near-wiped (Business Today, 2026).

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: STELINA digitizes documents but the initial sheet still relies on port officers transcribing what a captain declares; small vessels (the majority) largely sit outside e-logbook coverage (coverage share unverified). Processor-level records reconstruct provenance after mixing. In aquaculture, the eFis

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: The eFishery case is the strongest single-custodian-fraud story in the country: an operator falsifying its own database for six years is precisely the chain-shaped scenario. But the parties who needed proof (investors, auditors) buy audits, not protocols; and for trade compliance, flag-state certifi

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem without blockchain: YES — IUU, catch-cert fraud, fabricated farm data all persist. PASS.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator: the accepted model already — state registries (STELINA, SHTI) and processor systems; verifiers accept them. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: 3. Six-month ERP feature: Wholechain/Trace Register/ThisFish already sell SIMP- and GDST-compliant modules. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone economic value: sector WTP has collapsed — Aruna and FishLog cut staff for lack of margin, eFishery imploded; exporters treat documentation as a cost to minimize. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: Verdict: KILLED (fails 2, 3 and 4).

searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.text: - Market 4 — Indonesian fisheries traceability software spend plausibly under $100M (sizing unverified); export base ~$1B/quarter.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 4 — exporters minimize paperwork cost; startups serving the sector are all distressed; state budget slow.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 5 — multi-org, but flag state is the accepted trusted intermediary for every foreign verifier.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 5 — EO 14276 points to SIMP retrenchment, not expansion; no fresh deadline; eFishery scandal fading.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 5 — several attempts, none dominant, incumbents distressed — open but for bad reasons.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 4 — GDST standard exists; port/processor integrations give some lock-in.

searchIndex.title: Fisheries & Aquaculture Traceability (fisheries)
searchIndex.text: - Weighted: 5.0.

searchIndex.text: # Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: Under UU 33/2014 and PP 42/2024, halal certification is mandatory and state-run through BPJPH (Kemenag). Regular route: business obtains an NIB → applies in BPJPH's SIHALAL portal → selects an accredited LPH (halal inspection body) → halal auditors inspect ingredients, process and facility → finding

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: Deadlines: for medium/large food and beverage businesses, certification became mandatory 18 October 2024; micro and small enterprises (UMK) in food, beverage and slaughter must be certified by 17 October 2026 — a deadline roughly three months away as of this scan — with imported products also folded

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: Producers pay certification fees (or take free SEHATI quotas); BPJPH regulates, issues, and sanctions; 79 LPHs with about 1,740 registered halal auditors nationally (Kemenko PMK, 2024) do inspections — LPPOM MUI alone claims 1,000+ auditors (LPPOM, 2025); MUI holds the fatwa monopoly; P3H assistants

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - **Certified products containing pork, April 2025** — joint BPOM–BPJPH sampling found 9 processed foods with porcine DNA/peptides; 7 of them held valid halal certificates. Products were recalled under PP 42/2024 sanctions (BPOM press release; Kompas; Detik, April 2025). This is the core failure: th

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - **Self-declare abuse** — the 2023 "Nabidz" case, in which a wine-like product obtained a halal certificate via the self-declare route, triggered public criticism of the no-testing pathway (widely reported 2023; not re-verified in this session — (unverified)).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - **Structural gap** — self-declare certificates are issued in the millions (SEHATI quotas: 1 million free certificates in 2025, 1.35 million in 2026, per BPJPH) with no lab verification, while auditor capacity (~1,740) cannot physically inspect the long tail; LPPOM warned of 300–500% application qu

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: BPJPH certified 5,302,257 products during 2019–2024 (BPJPH, 2024) against a universe of ~62 million UMK (Kemenko PMK, 2024); only ~30% of UMKM held certificates by 2025 (Universitas Islam Indonesia halal center, 2025 — weak source). Certification fees for regular-route SMEs run roughly Rp 300 thousa

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - **Government:** SIHALAL (end-to-end digital certification and public certificate registry), SEHATI free-certificate program, BPJPH–BPOM joint market surveillance, BPJPH international mutual-recognition agreements.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - **Inspection ecosystem:** LPPOM MUI, Sucofindo, Surveyor Indonesia, university LPHs (79 total).

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - **Traceability tech:** as of this search, halal supply-chain blockchain in Indonesia exists only as academic frameworks and pilots (MDPI Economies 2022; MDPI Engineering Proceedings 2025; IEEE bibliometric survey 2025; ScienceDirect "HalalChain" model 2025). No funded Indonesian commercial halal-t

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: The certificate registry is already central, digital and authoritative (SIHALAL). What failed in April 2025 was not the registry but the link between certificate and physical product: self-declare skips testing, audits are point-in-time snapshots, and upstream ingredient changes after certification

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: Multi-party chain (ingredient suppliers → processors → LPH → MUI → BPJPH → foreign buyers) and genuine external verifiers (importing countries' halal authorities) fit the pattern. But an accepted neutral party exists and is legally unavoidable: BPJPH. Its registry is the ground truth by statute. A l

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain? **Yes.** Pass.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a single trusted operator? **Yes — SIHALAL is exactly that**, and the residual failures are physical, not custodial. Fail.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: 3. Incumbent ships it in 6 months? Certification workflow: already BPJPH's product. Traceability add-ons could be shipped by LPPOM or SIHALAL vendors, though none have. Partial fail.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone value? Weak — UMK cannot pay (state pays via SEHATI); LPHs are small buyers; only exporters have real WTP. Fail.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 7 — a certified-haram scandal in 2025 with recalls and regulatory exposure; reputational stakes for the whole regime.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - Market 5 — certification/integrity services around a multi-million-product mandate; tooling TAM plausibly $50–250M, unverified.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 4 — primary beneficiaries (UMK, consumers) cannot pay; the state gives certification away free; exporters are the only strong payers.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 5 — multi-org supply chain, but BPJPH/MUI are accepted (statutory) intermediaries.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 9 — the UMK mandatory deadline of 17 October 2026 is in force ~3 months out, with queue surges predicted.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 7 — hard search found only academic pilots for halal traceability; SIHALAL owns workflow, nobody owns integrity.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 5 — integration with SIHALAL/LPH workflows could lock in, but no cross-org network effect is guaranteed.

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: - **Weighted: 5.9**

searchIndex.title: Halal Certification Integrity (halal-certification)
searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.text: Killed on the kill test despite the best competition and urgency profile of this batch: the trust failure is physical (what is in the product) rather than informational (what the record says), the statutory central registry already exists, and the paying customer is missing — the state subsidizes pr
