searchIndex.text: # Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: JKN, run by BPJS Kesehatan, is the world's largest single-payer scheme. A hospital claim works like this: patient eligibility check and SEP (Surat Eligibilitas Peserta) issued through BPJS's V-Claim system → clinician documents care in the medical record → coder maps the episode to an INA-CBG tariff

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: Hospitals and clinics do the documentation and coding and carry cash-flow risk when claims pend. BPJS Kesehatan pays claims from a pool around Rp 150 trillion (2024, per KPK statements). Kemenkes sets tariffs and owns SATUSEHAT; BPKP and KPK audit; hospital associations (PERSI) dispute verification

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - **Phantom billing, July 2024** — the PK-JKN team found fictitious claims at 3 private hospitals: one in Central Java (Rp 29 billion) and two in North Sumatra (Rp 4 billion and Rp 1 billion), ~Rp 34 billion total; KPK took the case criminal (Kompas; Tempo; BPK Sumut, 2024). Actors included doctors

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - **Records vs claims mismatch, 2024** — at those hospitals, 4,341 physiotherapy claims vs 1,072 documented cases: 3,269 fictitious claims worth Rp 501.27 million; phantom physiotherapy was ~75% of case volume (CNBC Indonesia/KPK, 2024).

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - **Identity harvesting, 2024** — KPK described rings collecting KTP/BPJS numbers via fake community health events (baksos) to fabricate claims (Merdeka, 2024).

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - **Systemic estimate, Sept 2024** — KPK Deputy Chair Alexander Marwata: healthcare fraud losses ~Rp 20 trillion, roughly 10% of ~Rp 150 trillion in health funds, in some cases with facility staff cooperating with BPJS personnel (Monitor Indonesia; Tirto, 2024). This is an official's estimate, not a

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - **Response** — Kemenkes formed a dedicated fraud-prevention team and sanctions regime (Kemenkes/Sehat Negeriku, July 2024).

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: Fraud: ~Rp 20 trillion/year if the KPK estimate holds (KPK, 2024) — an order of magnitude above JKN's historical deficits. Verified floor: Rp 34 billion from just three hospitals (KPK/BPK, 2024). Administrative drag: claim pendings and disputes tie up hospital working capital (magnitude unverified).

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - **Government/payer:** BPJS V-Claim and Vedika (digital verification with rule-based screening), PK-JKN joint audit team, SATUSEHAT interoperability platform.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - **SIMRS/RME vendors** shipping SATUSEHAT integration: Infokes (eClinic), dHealth, and a crowded local SIMRS field.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - **AI fraud/claims tooling:** Badr Interactive sells healthcare fraud detection for the Indonesian ecosystem; Allianz Indonesia and Astra Life run AI claim automation; reinsurer Tugure pushes AI cost-containment (Infobank, 2026); insurers began deploying agentic AI for claims in 2026 (Bisnis.com, J

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: Detection is post-hoc and sample-based: the 2024 cases were caught by manually comparing claims against medical records — records the same hospital authors and can fabricate. There is no independent, time-stamped evidence that care events happened. SATUSEHAT moves data but does not make it trustwort

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: Superficially strong: adversarial parties (hospitals vs payer, even payer staff implicated) and external verifiers (KPK, BPKP, courts) who need proof independent of any custodian. But the dominant fraud mode is fabrication *at source* — a phantom patient is written into the record before any ledger

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain? **Yes.** Pass.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a single trusted operator? **Largely yes** — BPJS/Kemenkes are accepted operators; the binding constraint is analytics and enforcement capacity, not custodian trust. Fail.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: 3. Incumbent ships it in 6 months? **Plausible** — Vedika rule engines, SIMRS vendors, and AI vendors (Badr, insurer stacks) are already shipping fraud-detection features. Fail.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone value? The value pool is huge, but the buyer is one state payer with slow procurement. Marginal.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 9 — Rp 20T official fraud estimate, criminal cases, existential pressure on JKN finances.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - Market 5 — claims-integrity software TAM (payer procurement plus hospital SIMRS modules) plausibly $50–250M; no verified figure.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 6 — budget owners exist (BPJS, Kemenkes, insurers) and pay for inferior analytics, but the biggest buyer is slow state procurement.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 4 — multi-org and adversarial, yet accepted trusted intermediaries (BPJS, Kemenkes) run mandated central systems.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 7 — fresh 2024–2025 scandal, KPK cases live, SATUSEHAT enforcement tightening in 2026.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 4 — no dominant claims-integrity player, but BPJS internal systems plus active AI vendors and insurer stacks.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 4 — integration lock-in possible; core detection features are copyable.

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: - **Weighted: 5.8**

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.title: Health Records & BPJS Claims (healthcare-claims)
searchIndex.text: The kill already fired: fraud is fabricated at source, so tamper-evidence attacks the wrong link; the only buyer that matters (BPJS) trusts its own database and procures slowly; incumbent AI/SIMRS vendors can ship detection features faster than a startup can win a state contract. Watch item: if KPK/

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Hospitals/clinics and doctors generate claims; BPJS Kesehatan (282.7 million members, 2025) and ~140 licensed insurers pay; employers and members pay premiums; the state injects money when JKN runs deficits. Kemenkes sets tariffs and runs anti-fraud teams (Tim Pencegahan Kecurangan JKN, formed under

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia

searchIndex.text: - **Fraud prevalence estimate**: BPJS Kesehatan data presented at the First Indonesian Healthcare Anti-Fraud Forum put potential fraud at 0.6%–15% of total health financing (Media Indonesia, 2025) — a wide, weak range; treat as indicative only.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Trust context — investment-side scandals**: Jiwasraya, state loss Rp 16.81 trillion (BPK, 2020; three ex-directors sentenced to life); Asabri, state loss Rp 22.78 trillion (BPK, 2021; two ex-CEOs got 20 years). searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - JKN 2025: claims Rp 191.33 trillion vs premium income Rp 176.72 trillion; claims ratio 108.27%; deficit Rp 14.61 trillion (BPJS Kesehatan public expose via Kompas, July 2026). DJS deficit reported at Rp 17.13 trillion by Katadata (2026) on a different basis.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - If fraud is even 1% of JKN spending, that is ~Rp 1.9 trillion/year (arithmetic on BPJS 2025 figures; fraud share itself unverified).

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Private health claims paid: Rp 26.74 trillion in 2025, +9.1% y/y (AAJI via Readers.id, 2026).

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - KPK phantom-billing finding: Rp 34 billion across three hospitals (2024) — the audited tip, not the total.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07, named)

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **BPJS Kesehatan internal systems**: V-Claim submission, verification workflow, and a stated program to use AI for claims analysis and fraud prediction (GovInsider, 2024/2025).

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **State anti-fraud machinery**: KPK–Kemenkes–BPKP–BPJS joint monitoring team (active since 2017; the 2024 phantom-billing cases came from it); Kemenkes anti-fraud prevention teams and sanctions up to practice-license revocation (Kemenkes; Kompas, 2024).

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Regulation**: POJK 36/2025 (effective March 2026) mandating medical advisory boards, co-payment, and risk-sharing for private health insurance (OJK via Readers.id, 2026); OJK anti-fraud strategy rules for financial institutions.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Global vendors in-market**: Shift Technology's fraud detection deployed at Tokio Marine Indonesia since 2020 (Shift Technology, 2020); core systems and TPA analytics from AdMedika (Telkom) across cashless networks.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Insurtech**: Qoala, Rey, and others digitize distribution/claims UX (funding/traction numbers unverified).

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Verification is retrospective sampling on provider-authored documents: BPJS verifiers see the claim file, not the encounter, so phantom billing survives until a joint audit physically reconciles medical records — which happened for three hospitals out of ~3,100+ contracted (hospital count unverified

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: The data needed to catch fraud — medical records, claims, membership — already sits with BPJS or each insurer; detection is analytics inside one payer's perimeter. A cross-payer fraud registry would be multi-org, but OJK/Kemenkes are accepted authorities and could host it centrally. No external veri

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem persists without blockchain — PASS.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator (BPJS/OJK-hosted analytics and shared registry) solves it as well — FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 3. Six-month incumbent feature: Shift Technology, core-system vendors, and BPJS's own AI program already ship this — FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone value exists (deficit pressure) but the buyer is one state agency plus insurers served by incumbents.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: **KILLED on questions 2 and 3.**

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Severity 9 — 108% claims ratio, Rp 14.6T deficit, KPK criminal cases, and sector trust destroyed by Jiwasraya/Asabri.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Market 5 — anti-fraud/claims-analytics spend by BPJS plus ~140 insurers plausibly US$50–250M TAM; the loss pool is huge but not the software market.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - WTP 7 — quantified loss avoidance and deficit pressure; BPJS is a motivated but slow single government buyer.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Chain 3 — payer-side analytics on data the payer already holds; single trusted operator is fine.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 8 — deficit widened 124% in 2025 and POJK 36/2025 took effect March 2026; action is being forced now.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Competition 3 — Shift Technology live in Indonesia, BPJS building AI internally, global vendors abundant.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Moat 3 — detection models and registries are copyable features for incumbents with the data.

searchIndex.title: Insurance Claims & Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: **Weighted: 5.7** — below 7.0 cutoff and killed on the kill test.

searchIndex.text: # Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Productive (business) P2P lending and invoice financing work like this: (1) an SME borrower uploads an invoice or purchase order owed by a payor (often a large corporate or government buyer); (2) the platform or bank verifies the borrower's identity (KTP, NPWP), pulls SLIK/credit-bureau data, checks

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Platform credit/risk teams do the verification; ~94 licensed platforms (OJK, 2026). Retail and institutional lenders (including banks channeling via P2P) bear losses. Borrowing SMEs pay interest of the whole stack. OJK licenses and supervises (POJK 10/POJK.05/2022); AFPI self-regulates and runs the

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Investree, 2023–2025**: TWP90 hit 16.44% against OJK's 5% limit; OJK revoked the license on 21 October 2024 (KEP-53/D.06/2024) for equity violations and deteriorating performance, declared co-founder/CEO Adrian Gunadi unfit, referred criminal suspicions to law enforcement; Gunadi fled, got an In

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **KoinWorks/KoinP2P borrower fraud, 2024**: borrower "MT" obtained Rp 365 billion using forged KTP data — one scheme used 279 identity cards — then absconded (Suara/Merdeka, 2024).

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **KoinWorks fictitious-invoice case, 2024–2026**: prosecutors allege Rp 600 billion of bank funds (reported as BRI money channeled through the platform) was disbursed to fictitious borrowers using fake invoices for companies with no real transactions; three current/former directors named suspects

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **TaniFund**: defaults from late 2022 (TKB90 reached 50%); license revoked 3 May 2024; lender suits over Rp 3.04 billion and Rp 2.57 billion losses (Kontan; Kompas, 2024). **iGrow (LinkAja group)**: defaults since June 2023; 40 lenders sued for Rp 3.18 billion material losses (Katadata, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Rp 2.7 trillion alleged illegal fund-raising, Investree case (OJK/Detik, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Rp 365 billion + Rp 600 billion, the two KoinWorks cases (police/prosecutors via Suara 2024, Media Indonesia 2026).

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Industry TWP90 4.62% of Rp 102 trillion outstanding ≈ Rp 4.7 trillion 90-day-delinquent at April 2026 (OJK, 2026) — default, not all fraud.

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Sector-wide annual fraud-specific losses: (unverified) — no named aggregate exists.

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Indirect cost: lender confidence; the PTUN lawsuits against OJK (Katadata, 2025) and license revocations of 4 platforms in 2024 (Tempo, 2024) evidence systemic trust damage.

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07, named)

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **AFPI Fintech Data Center (FDC)** and **OJK Pusdafil**: mandatory daily borrower-level data submission; platforms must check FDC before lending to catch duplicate *borrowers* across platforms (AFPI; Kompas, 2019; World Bank FSAP, 2024).

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **SLIK (OJK)**: bank-and-finance-company debtor registry.

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **AHU Online fidusia registry** (Kemenkumham): registers fiduciary deeds over receivables; deed-level, notary-mediated, not searchable by invoice.

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **DJP e-Faktur/Coretax**: tax e-invoices with QR validation exist for VAT-registered firms — a government authenticity rail, not connected to lending (general knowledge; integration status unverified).

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **MonetaGo**: partnered with FCI for invoice-finance dedup globally and runs Singapore's registry (GTR, 2023); no Indonesian deployment found.

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Credit insurers/guarantors** (Askrindo, Jamkrindo) absorb some default risk (roles per general knowledge, unverified specifics).

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: FDC/Pusdafil match on borrower identity, not on documents: the same invoice financed at two platforms under two borrowing entities, or a wholly fabricated invoice, passes every existing check. Fidusia registration is optional in practice for small facilities, costs notary fees, and cannot reveal dou

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Multi-lender, adversarial borrowers, and real double-pledging — the strongest chain case of the three. But every lender answers to OJK, and AFPI already operates a trusted shared utility (FDC); extending it to hashed invoice fingerprints is an ordinary database feature. Singapore's centralized regis

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem exists without blockchain — PASS.

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator: an invoice-hash registry run by AFPI/OJK (or MonetaGo) solves it — FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 3. Six-month incumbent feature: AFPI could extend FDC to invoice-level; MonetaGo could enter via FCI members — borderline FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone economic value — plausible (per-check fees across Rp 34T productive lending) but thin against a utility priced at cost.

searchIndex.title: Invoice Financing & P2P Lending Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: **KILLED on question 2 (and likely 3).**

searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.text: - Severity 8 — license revocations, a fugitive CEO, criminal prosecutions of directors; existential for platforms.

searchIndex.text: - Market 5 — verification/registry revenue on Rp 34.6T productive P2P plus bank invoice financing lands in the US$50–250M band.

searchIndex.text: - WTP 7 — platforms already pay for FDC/bureau checks and bear direct quantified fraud losses; clear budget owner.

searchIndex.text: - Chain 4 — multi-org but OJK/AFPI are accepted neutral operators with a live shared utility.

searchIndex.text: - Competition 6 — FDC/Pusdafil solve the adjacent borrower-level problem; invoice-level dedup is open but MonetaGo/FCI loom.

searchIndex.text: - Moat 5 — integration lock-in with platforms; the association could commoditize it.

searchIndex.text: AFPI adding invoice-hash fields to FDC; OJK mandating invoice verification against Coretax/e-Faktur data (the state already holds the authoritative invoice record); MonetaGo entering with FCI members. searchIndex.text: Zakat: a muzakki (payer) either gives directly to recipients/mosques, or pays through the official system — BAZNAS (national, provincial, district) and licensed LAZ (amil institutions). searchIndex.text: Muzakki/wakif fund everything; amil institutions (BAZNAS units, 30+ national LAZ, thousands of local amil) do the work and keep the amil share; Kemenag regulates and sharia-audits; public accountants audit larger OPZ; DPR Commission VIII and donors dispute performance; heirs and local governments di

searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Islamic Social Finance — Zakat & Waqf Transparency
searchIndex.text: - ACT (Aksi Cepat Tanggap), 2022: Kemensos revoked the fundraising licence of one of Indonesia's largest philanthropy institutions after findings that donated funds were diverted to executive pay and unrelated ventures (Kemensos/PPATK, 2022). It reset public suspicion of all intermediated giving.

searchIndex.title: Islamic Social Finance — Zakat & Waqf Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Waqf land: of 522,000+ parcels recorded in SIWAK, only 58.76% are certified (ATR/BPN via Kompas.com, 2026); in East Java 51.87% of 78,825 parcels lack certificates (Kemenag/KPK, 2025). Uncertified parcels are recurrently disputed or reclaimed by heirs when the wakif dies — Kompas (2026) documents

searchIndex.title: Islamic Social Finance — Zakat & Waqf Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Donor distrust: Indonesian academic surveys (JOIPAD 2023; ResearchGate/IAIN studies) consistently find muzakki prefer direct giving to mosques/mustahik, viewing it as more afdhal and distrusting institutional competence; no single verified national percentage exists (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Islamic Social Finance — Zakat & Waqf Transparency
searchIndex.text: - The collection gap itself: potential Rp327.6 trillion/year (BAZNAS IPPZ methodology, 2019, using 2016-2018 data) versus ~10% realized (BAZNAS via Antara, 2024-2025).

searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Islamic Social Finance — Zakat & Waqf Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Government: SIMBA (mandated recording + DJP tax integration), SIWAK (waqf land registry), KPK-Kemenag-BPN certification drives, CWLS (Cash Waqf Linked Sukuk retail series, e.g., SWR006 marketed by Bank Mega Syariah with a Rp15 billion target — BWI, Oct 2025).

searchIndex.title: Islamic Social Finance — Zakat & Waqf Transparency

searchIndex.text: - Blockchain-specific: Finterra's WAQF Chain pilot (2018), a Telkom-BWI blockchain use case (2020), and a steady stream of Indonesian academic prototypes (BWI's own journal, 2022-2025). None has reached production scale; the literature itself frames adoption as unresolved.

searchIndex.title: Islamic Social Finance — Zakat & Waqf Transparency

searchIndex.text: # Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: A Koperasi Simpan Pinjam (KSP) takes mandatory and voluntary savings (simpanan pokok, wajib, sukarela) from members and lends to members. Governance runs through the annual members' meeting (RAT), which approves the board's self-prepared financial statements. External oversight is a reporting relati

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: Members (savers/borrowers) bear the losses; boards and managers do the work; Kemenkop/dinas and now OJK supervise; courts and PKPU (suspension-of-payments) administrators handle disputes. Payers for any solution would be: cooperatives themselves (weak payers), the state (Kemenkop, OJK, Kopdes progra

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - KSP Indosurya: member losses of Rp16 trillion per the prosecution (Viva, 2022; prosecutors' filing); acquitted at Jakarta Barat District Court (Jan 2023), then the Supreme Court cassation (No. 2113 K/Pid.Sus/2023, 16 May 2023) sentenced founder Henry Surya to 18 years and a Rp15 billion fine; June

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Eight problem cooperatives (Indosurya, Sejahtera Bersama Rp8.6T, Intidana Rp930B, Lima Garuda Rp570B, Timur Pratama Rp400B, both Pracico entities ~Rp1.39T, Wahana Berkah Sentosa Rp226B) defaulted on Rp26 trillion of member claims (Kemenkop via Antara/CNBC, 2023); only Rp3.4 trillion had been repai

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Kopdes Merah Putih: a CELIOS survey of 108 village heads across 34 provinces found ~65% saw large governance gaps, warning of "structured corruption" risk (CELIOS/The Conversation, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: The recurring pattern: books shown to members and to ODS diverge from actual fund positions; RAT approval is captured; PKPU is then used to freeze claims.

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: Rp26 trillion in defaulted claims across eight cooperatives, ~Rp22.6 trillion still unpaid as of 2024 (Kemenkop via Tempo). Indosurya alone: Rp16 trillion (prosecution, 2022). State fiscal exposure from the 80,000-cooperative Kopdes program is flagged by DPR and CNBC opinion analyses (2025) but unqu

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Government: Kemenkop ODS / ODS Mandiri (self-reporting); OJK licensing and supervision of open-loop cooperatives (in force since Jan 2025); RUU Perkoperasian (4th amendment) in DPR — the government submitted its DIM in June 2026, proposing an LPS Koperasi (deposit guarantee) and a dedicated Kopdes

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Vendors: PT USSI (IBS/IBSS core banking; claims 1,730+ institutions including BPR/BPRS, BMT, cooperatives; engaged in Kopdes gerai rollout with Kemenkop, 2026), Smartcoop (400+ cooperatives), eKoperasi, Koperasiweb, MyKopkel, and custom-build shops. All offer member apps, automated bookkeeping, an

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - No dedicated Indonesian startup was found selling independent, member-facing verification of KSP solvency; the market sells management software, not assurance.

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: ODS ingests whatever the cooperative types in; nothing reconciles reported balances with actual bank/cash positions. Vendor core-banking systems are bought by, and answer to, the same management that commits the fraud. OJK covers only 21 open-loop entities so far. LPS Koperasi does not yet exist. So

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: The fraud is intra-organizational: management vs. members, with the regulator as an accepted (if under-resourced) neutral party. A regulator-run database with mandatory core-banking integration — effectively what OJK does for banks — addresses the problem without distributed trust. Tamper-evidence o

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem exists without blockchain: YES. 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator (OJK/Kemenkop + mandated reporting): YES, it would solve it — FAIL. 3. Incumbent vendors (USSI, Smartcoop) or the state could ship member-visibility features within six months: plausibly YES — FAIL. 4. Standalone value

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Severity 9 — Rp26T documented member losses, criminal convictions, existential for the sector (Kemenkop 2023).

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Market 5 — ~130k cooperatives but low software ARPU; supervision-tech TAM plausibly $50-250M (unverified basis).

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - WTP 5 — state budget and program money exist (Kopdes, OJK), but procurement is slow; cooperatives themselves pay little.

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Chain 4 — multi-party but an accepted trusted intermediary (OJK) exists and is expanding.

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 9 — OJK transition in force, RUU Perkoperasian with LPS Koperasi in DPR now, 80k Kopdes live: deadline pressure is current.

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Competition 4 — entrenched vendors (USSI 1,730 institutions) plus free government systems.

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Moat 4 — integration lock-in possible, no structural network effect.

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: - Weighted: 5.9

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.title: Koperasi — Savings Cooperative (KSP) Transparency
searchIndex.text: It is already killed as a blockchain venture: the state is building the trusted-operator solution (OJK + LPS Koperasi), and incumbents own the integration surface. A pure supervision-SaaS play competes with free ODS and politically driven procurement.

searchIndex.text: # Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: Researched 2026-07-29. Phase 1 scan, pre-committed rubric.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: Land registration is a state monopoly of Kementerian ATR/BPN under PP 24/1997 (amended by PP 18/2021). First-time registration runs either sporadically (owner applies at the local land office) or systematically through PTSL, the mass-titling program running since 2017. Steps: application with basis-

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: Status mid-2026: 126.55 million parcels registered by April 2026 (125.6 million by end-2025, of which 97.4 million certificated) (ATR/BPN via Bisnis.com/Infopriangan, 2025–2026). Electronic certificates: all land offices implement issuance since October 2024, but only 7.6 million e-certificates exis

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - ATR/BPN and ~480 land offices: operate the registry; government budget pays.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - PPAT/notaries: gatekeep transactions, charge fees.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Village/kelurahan officials: hold pre-registration records (letter C) — a recurring fraud vector.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Banks: rely on certificates as collateral; pay HT-el and checking fees.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Buyers, developers, and citizens: bear fraud losses; courts (PN/PTUN) and the Satgas Anti-Mafia Tanah (ATR/BPN + Polri + Kejaksaan, since 2018) handle disputes.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Mbah Tupon case (Bantul, 2025): a 68-year-old illiterate farmer's 1,655 m² certificate was transferred to another name and pledged for a Rp1.5 billion loan without his knowledge; seven perpetrators including a former village head/DPRD member were arrested April 2025 and convicted November 2025; ce

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Malang double certificates (2025): BPN Kabupaten Malang issued a 2024 SHM over land already covered by a 1994 SHM held by residents for 30 years; dozens reported the case to Polda Jatim (Beritajatim, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Satgas Anti-Mafia Tanah 2025 results: 90 cases resolved (target 65), 185 suspects named, Rp23.38 trillion in potential state losses averted, 14,315 ha of land saved (ATR/BPN via detik/Harianjogja, December 2025).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Case load: 3,260 land dispute/conflict cases recorded through September 2025 (detik, November 2025); 6,015 cases received October 2024–October 2025, 50.02% resolved (ATR/BPN, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Double and forged certificates persist into the e-certificate era (Tatkala, June 2026).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Rp23.38 trillion potential losses averted by the anti-mafia task force in 2025 alone (ATR/BPN, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Rp9.67 trillion in potential losses saved via dispute/conflict resolution October 2024–October 2025 (ATR/BPN, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Individual exposure is existential: single-family losses of Rp1.5 billion+ (Mbah Tupon, 2025). Aggregate private losses, litigation cost, and collateral-value drag: (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - ATR/BPN's own modernization: sertifikat elektronik (Permen ATR 3/2023), Sentuh Tanahku app, BHUMI map portal, HT-el electronic mortgage, electronic certificate checking for PPATs, PTSL mass titling (~4.3 million parcels/year average; 2026 target 1.87 million after budget cuts — Bisnis.com, 2025/20

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Satgas Anti-Mafia Tanah (enforcement, not prevention).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Blockchain: academic pilots and readiness studies only (STPN journals, UI thesis); ministerial roadmap statements for 2028. No verified production system.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Meridia (Netherlands): smallholder land documentation in Indonesia for agri supply chains (EUDR-driven) — parcel mapping, not registry integrity (Common Fund for Commodities; meridia.land).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Manual due-diligence services (law firms, e.g., Putranto Alliance certificate verification).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: Every safeguard runs through the same custodian. The fraud pattern is insider-mediated: village heads, rogue notaries, and compromised land-office processes produce genuine-looking (or genuinely issued) conflicting certificates. E-certificates centralize the record further without giving citizens, b

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: This is the strongest chain fit of the three: multi-party (BPN, notaries, banks, courts, citizens), the custodian itself is the distrusted element, and external verifiers need proof independent of the record-keeper — a genuine anchor-7+ scenario. A PostgreSQL under BPN is exactly what exists and exa

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain? YES (passes).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a single trusted operator? NO — the operator (BPN) is the party whose integrity is in question (passes).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 3. Incumbent ERP feature in 6 months? NO (passes).

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 4. Enough value for a standalone company? NO — only BPN can legally operate the registry; a private tamper-evidence layer has no legal force in court or at a bank. The venture collapses into winning a politically fraught government IT procurement against an incumbent state program already funded and

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 9 — documented mass fraud, Rp23T-scale exposure, existential losses for victims, criminal syndicates.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Market 5 — government land-IT budget plus bank due-diligence spend plausibly $50–250M TAM for a vendor; (unverified) precisely.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 3 — victims (citizens) cannot pay; government procurement is slow and political; banks pay only small checking fees.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 7 — multi-org, no accepted neutral party besides the distrusted custodian; independent verifiability would change bank and court behavior.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 7 — conversion of 89.4M paper certificates is in force now; fresh scandals (Mbah Tupon) keep political attention high.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 4 — the funded incumbent with traction is the state's own e-certificate program; competing means displacing or supplying it.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 5 — a mandate would confer protocol position, but that mandate is the unobtainable part.

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.title: Land Titles & BPN (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: Already killed on standalone-company grounds. It would revive only if ATR/BPN formally procured an independent anchoring/verification layer (the 2028 blockchain roadmap becoming a funded tender) — worth monitoring, not building ahead of.

searchIndex.title: Mining Provenance & Quotas (Nickel, Coal)

searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Mining Provenance & Quotas (Nickel, Coal)
searchIndex.text: - **"Dokumen terbang" (flying documents):** legal RKAB documents are rented out to launder ore from unlicensed pits into smelters; laundered ore trades 10–12.5% below official ore and evades royalty, tax and environmental funds. The practice was reported as rampant again in 2026, driven by the quota

searchIndex.title: Mining Provenance & Quotas (Nickel, Coal)
searchIndex.text: - **Antam Mandiodo case:** illegal ore sales from the Mandiodo block, Southeast Sulawesi, using fraudulent RKAB documents; state loss estimated at Rp 5.7 trillion (Kejaksaan Agung, 2023). Eight defendants sentenced April 2024, including former Minerba Director-General Ridwan Djamaludin (Kejaksaan; T

searchIndex.title: Mining Provenance & Quotas (Nickel, Coal)
searchIndex.text: - **Illegal exports:** KPK found 5.3 Mt of nickel ore shipped to China during 2020–June 2022 despite the export ban, worth ~Rp 14.5 trillion (US$963M), detected via BPS–China customs data discrepancy (KPK; Tempo/Indonesia Business Post, 2023).

searchIndex.title: Mining Provenance & Quotas (Nickel, Coal)
searchIndex.text: - **Scale:** Bareskrim mapped 1,517 illegal mining (PETI) sites across 33 provinces in 2025 (Bisnis, Dec 2025). In February 2026, four Maluku Utara nickel miners were fined for mining outside license areas — one fined Rp 2.27 trillion for 234 ha (Mongabay Indonesia, 2026).

searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Mining Provenance & Quotas (Nickel, Coal)
searchIndex.text: - **Government:** SIMBARA (fiscal/transaction gatekeeping, 5 commodities by 2026), MODI/MOMS/e-RKAB (licensing, production reporting).

searchIndex.title: Mining Provenance & Quotas (Nickel, Coal)
searchIndex.text: - **Global vendors:** Circulor (battery-passport traceability; partnerships with Talon Metals, Acculon/Rockwell — no verified Indonesian deployment found), RCS Global/SLR, Minespider. IRMA third-party mine audits are underway at some Indonesian facilities under carmaker pressure (Ford Conflict Miner

searchIndex.title: Mining Provenance & Quotas (Nickel, Coal)
searchIndex.text: - **Indonesian:** Baliola (Mandala Chain, Bali) pitches blockchain mineral traceability and won Startup World Cup Indonesia (Baliola, 2025) — pre-traction. Surveyors (Sucofindo, Surveyor Indonesia) remain the incumbent verification layer.

searchIndex.title: Mining Provenance & Quotas (Nickel, Coal)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Mining Provenance & Quotas (Nickel, Coal)
searchIndex.text: SIMBARA verifies that a shipment has valid documents and paid royalties; it does not verify that the ore physically came from the licensed pit — which is exactly the fraud (dokumen terbang persisted into 2026). Surveyor certificates are point-in-time, bribable, and not machine-verifiable downstream.

searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: Authentic deeds (akta autentik) — company incorporations, land sale deeds (AJB via PPAT), credit agreements, wills — must be executed before a notary: parties appear physically, sign the minuta with fingerprints, the notary keeps the protocol (paper archive) and issues salinan (copies). Company deed

searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: Roughly 3,000 notaries practice in Central Java alone (Kemenkum Jateng, April 2025); the national figure is commonly put above 20,000 (unverified). Parties to transactions pay notary fees; banks pay for credit and collateral deeds; companies pay for corporate acts. Oversight: Majelis Pengawas (MPD/M

searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents, cited)

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Forged deeds are the operating tool of the land mafia. ATR/BPN uncovered 86 land-mafia cases with 159 suspects in 2023, claiming Rp13.2 trillion in potential losses averted (Kompas, March 2024); the Grobogan case alone was valued at Rp3.41 trillion and the Dago Elos/Bandung case at Rp3.65 trillion

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Notaries as perpetrators: a Gresik notary/PPAT was arrested in 2025 for forging survey documents and signatures that shrank a victim's certified land by thousands of square meters (detik, 2025); a Malang notary was reported to police for deed forgery and double sale after MPD channels failed (Suar

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - e-Meterai stress: during CASN 2024 registration Peruri's e-meterai site failed for days, spawning warnings about counterfeit e-meterai sold by third parties; Peruri published visual authenticity checks (CNBC Indonesia, Sept 2024; Jawa Pos, 2024).

searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Land-mafia potential losses in one year's uncovered cases: Rp13.2 trillion (ATR/BPN via Kompas, 2024). Deed forgery is a core enabling step in these schemes.

searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07, named)

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - State systems: AHU Online (incorporation, fidusia, wasiat), apostille.ahu.go.id with QR-verifiable certificates, e-Meterai (Peruri monopoly), IKD/PSrE signatures for private documents.

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Licensed PSrE (Privy, VIDA, Peruri) provide legally valid electronic signatures — but these cannot produce an authentic notarial deed under current UUJN.

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Legaltech: Kontrak Hukum, Legalku and similar startups broker incorporation and notary services online; they digitize intake, not deed integrity.

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Verification: no national public registry lets a bank or buyer cryptographically verify an arbitrary deed's existence and content; checking means asking the notary or Kemenkumham. No funded Indonesian startup doing deed integrity/verification was found (searched; absence of evidence, mid-2026).

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: The forgery surface survives digitization because the authentic-deed layer is legally locked to paper: protocols sit in notary offices, salinan can be fabricated, and third parties have no independent verification path. AHU registers outcomes (company data) but not deed contents; apostille verifies

searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: Multi-party, adversarial, and courts need proof — superficially a fit. But Indonesia has an accepted, legally exclusive trust operator for exactly this layer: the state. Kemenkumham could add a hash-registry to AHU; Peruri's e-Meterai monopoly shows the state claims document-trust infrastructure for

searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain: YES. 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator just as good: YES — fails. A central deed-hash registry run by Kemenkumham (which already runs AHU/apostille) solves verification; courts would accept it precisely because it is the state's. 3. Incumbent ships in 6 m

searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 8 — forged authentic deeds enable trillion-rupiah land fraud and criminal exposure for parties and notaries (ATR/BPN 2024; detik 2025).

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Market 4 — notary fees are large in aggregate, but the addressable software/verification slice is well under $250M (unverified, conservative).

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 4 — 20k+ fragmented small offices; banks would pay but expect the state to provide the registry.

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 5 — multi-org with an accepted trusted intermediary (Kemenkumham/Peruri) exactly matching the anchor.

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 5 — recurring mafia-tanah scandals create pressure, but UUJN revision has been "coming" for a decade with no deadline.

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 6 — no private player owns deed verification; only state systems and incorporation brokers; pilots/whitespace but for structural reasons.

searchIndex.title: Notarial Deeds & Document Legalization (notary-civil-docs)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 4 — workflow integration with notary offices is sticky, yet the state can subsume the trust layer at any time.

searchIndex.text: Weighted: 5.3

searchIndex.title: Palm Oil Traceability (palm-oil)
searchIndex.text: Multi-party and adversarial (mills vs regulators vs NGOs vs EU buyers), and the state custodian is conflicted — that argues for tamper-evidence. But the EU accepts centrally filed DDS; certification bodies and state surveyors are accepted intermediaries; and the dominant failure is fabricated or abs

searchIndex.title: Palm Oil Traceability (palm-oil)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Palm Oil Traceability (palm-oil)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem without blockchain: YES — EUDR and illegal-FFB laundering persist. PASS.

searchIndex.title: Palm Oil Traceability (palm-oil)
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator: would largely solve it — Surveyor Indonesia and Koltiva are accepted operators today. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Palm Oil Traceability (palm-oil)

searchIndex.title: Palm Oil Traceability (palm-oil)
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone value: yes for the category, but it is being captured by incumbents. PASS.

searchIndex.title: Palm Oil Traceability (palm-oil)
searchIndex.text: Verdict: KILLED (fails 2 and 3).

searchIndex.title: Palm Oil Traceability (palm-oil)

searchIndex.text: # Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: Indonesia's drug supply chain runs manufacturer → licensed distributor (PBF) → pharmacy/hospital, governed by BPOM. Every product needs a marketing authorization (NIE); distributors need CDOB (good distribution practice) certification; hospital purchasing for JKN runs through LKPP's e-katalog, whose

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: Serialization is already regulated. PerBPOM 33/2018, revised by PerBPOM 22/2022, mandates 2D barcodes in two tiers: an *identification* barcode (NIE + product identity) for OTC, traditional medicine, supplements, cosmetics and processed food, effective 7 December 2023; and an *authentication* barcod

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: Manufacturers (Kimia Farma, Kalbe, Dexa, multinationals) pay for serialization lines and TTAC reporting; PBF distributors pay for scanning/aggregation; pharmacies and hospitals do the work of verification; BPOM audits and prosecutes with Polri; Kemenkes/BPJS pay for drugs via e-katalog and bear the

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - **Vaksin palsu, 2016** — Bareskrim raided a fake-vaccine ring (Pondok Aren, 22 June 2016); the Health Minister named 14 hospitals and 8 midwives/clinics that administered fake vaccines; roughly 20–25 suspects were charged (Hukumonline; Detik, 2016). The defining proof that counterfeits penetrated

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - **Illegal online channel, 2025** — BPOM reported 197,725 links selling illegal drugs/food during 2025 with claimed "potential economic value" of Rp 49.82 trillion (BPOM, 2025; methodology for the valuation is opaque — treat as an upper-bound agency claim). 14,787 takedown recommendations 2022–Sept

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - **Illegal warehouse, Oct 2025** — BPOM and Polda Metro Jaya seized an illegal pharma warehouse in West Jakarta, evidence valued Rp 2.74 billion including illegal propofol (BPOM, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - **Recurring counterfeits, 2025–2026** — BPOM named 8 frequently counterfeited drugs (Ponstan, Tramadol, etc.) (Kompas, Feb 2026). Casework: 107 cases (2023), 120 (2024), 76 through Sept 2025 (BPOM).

searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: Indonesia's pharma market: IDR 176.3 trillion (~USD 11 billion) projected for 2025 (Fitch Ratings, cited by Asian Insiders, 2025). Counterfeit/illegal-channel losses: no credible verified annual figure; BPOM's Rp 49.82 trillion "potential value" (2025) is a link-count extrapolation, not measured sal

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - **Government:** BPOM TTAC (central serialization repository), BPOM Mobile verification app, e-katalog procurement records.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - **Global serialization vendors actively selling Indonesia compliance:** TraceLink (dedicated Indonesia compliance product), Antares Vision/rfxcel, Utrace, LSPedia, Jekson Vision, plus SAP ATTP inside multinationals.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - **Local/regional integrators:** Sun Teknovation (offline TTAC serialization up to 220 cartons/min), WINS (TTAC connector). Pharmacy SaaS (Farmacare) rides the compliance wave downstream.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: The gap is not record integrity — it is coverage and enforcement. TTAC covers the legal chain; the counterfeit economy lives in unserialized online marketplaces and informal resellers, where no barcode regime reaches. Downstream scanning discipline at pharmacies and consumer verification adoption ar

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: Adversaries exist (counterfeiters), but the verifier everyone accepts is the regulator itself. TTAC is precisely a central database under a single trusted operator, mandated by law; manufacturers, distributors, courts and consumers all defer to it. Tamper-evidence of supply-chain records is not the

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain? **Yes** (counterfeits are physical). Pass.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: 2. Would PostgreSQL under a single trusted operator solve it? **Yes — it already exists (TTAC/BPOM).** Fail.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: 3. Could an incumbent ship it in 6 months? **Effectively already shipped** — TraceLink, Antares Vision, Utrace, LSPedia sell Indonesia compliance today. Fail.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone company value? Compliance spend exists but is being captured by entrenched vendors. Marginal.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 7 — documented scandals (2016 vaccines) and recurring enforcement caseload, but day-to-day losses for legal-chain players are contained.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - Market 5 — serialization/compliance software TAM is a thin slice of the USD 11B drug market; no verified figure, plausibly $50–250M cumulative.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 7 — mandated compliance spend with hard deadlines, but budget owners are already paying incumbent vendors.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 3 — accepted trusted intermediary (BPOM) with a mandated central repository.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 7 — Dec 2025 deadline in force, Dec 2027 deadline inside 24 months.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 3 — multiple funded global incumbents with Indonesia-specific products and traction.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 3 — a new entrant's connector is a copyable feature.

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: - **Weighted: 5.2**

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.title: Pharma Track & Trace (pharma-supply)
searchIndex.text: Already killed: the trusted-operator registry exists and is law; the competitive space is occupied by global serialization vendors; the residual counterfeit problem is physical enforcement, which software of any architecture does not solve.

searchIndex.text: # Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: Indonesian government procurement runs through a mature, mandatory digital stack operated by LKPP. Each agency publishes its annual procurement plan in SiRUP; routine purchases go through e-Katalog (e-purchasing), and works or complex services go through competitive tender on SPSE via ~600 local LPS

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: The integrity problem is not data availability. LKPP publishes datasets (data.lkpp.go.id), the ISB API exposes tender data, and the open-source pyproc project (wakataw/pyproc, GitHub) already turns SPSE/Inaproc data into MCP tools for LLM agents. The gap is methodology and consequence: turning publi

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: Work is done by PPK, Pokja, and procurement units (UKPBJ) in ~86,000 spending units; vendors bid; LKPP operates the platforms. Auditors: APIP/inspektorat (internal), BPKP, BPK (external), KPK and police (criminal). Disputes: losing bidders via sanggah, KPPU for bid-rigging cartels. The payer for any

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents, cited)

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - ICW recorded 1,189 procurement corruption cases with 2,898 suspects in 2019–2023, dominant modes: fictitious projects, mark-up, fictitious reports, bribery (ICW via Kompas, June 2025).

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - KPK: 446 of 1,782 cases handled since 2004 through Dec 2025 — 25% — are procurement-related (KPK spokesperson, April 2026).

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - Tulungagung OTT, April 2026: KPK arrested 18 people including the bupati; collusion to steer e-Katalog awards was arranged through "communication outside the system"; KPK publicly demanded total evaluation of e-Katalog (Antara, May 2026).

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - ICW/OCP: 1,586 procurement corruption cases 2016–2022, ~US$2.7B state losses (Open Contracting Partnership, 2024).

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: The signature failure mode: the platform record is clean while the deal is dirty. Steering, HPS inflation, and bid rigging are agreed offline; the system faithfully records the staged outcome.

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - Potential state losses from procurement corruption 2019–2023: Rp47.18 trillion (ICW, reported June 2025).

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - Procurement spend at risk: RUP 2024 totaled Rp1,259.2 trillion (LKPP via DPR/emedia, 2025); e-Katalog transactions reached Rp123.3 trillion (LKPP via Tempo, 2025) and Rp56.03 trillion with 18.9 million listed products as of October 2025 (DPR emedia, Oct 2025).

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - Efficiency loss share of contract value: (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07, named)

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - LKPP itself: SPSE, SiRUP, SIKAP vendor profiles, e-Katalog V6 with tracked approvals; actively iterating with KPK on V6 anti-corruption design (Antara, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - Opentender.net (ICW + LKPP): public red-flag analytics using ICW's Potential Fraud Analysis across national and local tenders (OCP/ICW, 2021–2025).

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - BPKP/APIP probity audit framework (Perka BPKP 3/2019) — real-time procurement audits.

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - pyproc (open source, 2025): SPSE data as MCP tools; confirms data access is commoditized.

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - BPK e-audit and KPK's MCP/Stranas PK dashboards (partial, government-internal).

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - No funded Indonesian startup selling procurement-integrity analytics was found; the space is occupied by state bodies and civil society, not companies.

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: Red-flag analytics exist but produce leads, not consequences; follow-through depends on APIP capacity and political will. V6 closes workflow gaps yet the Tulungagung case shows collusion simply moved off-platform. The binding constraints are enforcement incentives and auditor capacity — neither is a

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: Records in SPSE are not being tampered with after the fact; they are truthful records of corrupted decisions. Tamper-evidence therefore changes nothing. LKPP is a functioning, accepted single operator; a PostgreSQL-backed audit trail under LKPP (which already exists) captures everything a chain woul

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain: YES (it is a collusion problem). 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator just as good: YES — fails. LKPP is that operator today. 3. Incumbent ships it in 6 months: YES — fails. LKPP iterates V6 continuously and owns the mandate. 4. Standalone company value: NO

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 9 — Rp47.18T documented losses, 25% of all KPK cases (ICW 2025; KPK 2026).

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - Market 3 — TAM for integrity tooling (agency audit budgets + donors) plausibly under $50M; procurement spend itself is not addressable revenue.

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 3 — beneficiary is the public; agency buyers have weak incentive to purchase self-exposure.

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 3 — single accepted operator (LKPP) exists; falsification happens off-system.

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 7 — fresh scandal (Tulungagung, April 2026) and KPK pressure, but pressure lands on LKPP, not on a startup's buyer.

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 5 — Opentender.net, BPKP probity audit, pyproc: several attempts, none commercial, none dominant.

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 3 — public data, publishable methodology; copyable.

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: Weighted: 4.8

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.title: Public Procurement Integrity (procurement)
searchIndex.text: Already killed: no paying customer with aligned incentives, LKPP as accepted operator, fraud executed off-ledger, and personal legal risk to the operator of an accusatory analytics product.

searchIndex.text: # Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: Health: under UU Kesehatan 17/2023, every medical and health worker needs an STR (registration) and an SIP (practice permit). STR is now lifetime; SIP is renewed every 5 years against SKP (CPD credit) requirements. Applications run digitally through SATUSEHAT SDMK, launched 11 October 2023 (Kemenkes

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: Practitioners pay registration and certification fees (SKK costs are borne by workers or contractors). Hospitals and clinics pay credentialing staff time; contractors pay compliance staff for tender document assembly; clients of lawyers have no practical verification channel. Regulators: Konsil Kese

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Susanto, a non-doctor who worked roughly two years at a Pertamina site clinic using a real doctor's identity documents, was sentenced to 3.5 years on 19 March 2024 (ResearchGate case review; Merdeka, 2024). The registry entry he exploited was genuine — the fraud was identity substitution, which no

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Bekasi, 2024: a fake doctor practiced for five years on forged SIP and STR before arrest (Merdeka, 2024).

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Bantul, 2024–2025: a fake medical practitioner defrauded a patient of Rp538.95 million plus a land certificate (Polres Bantul, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Lombok Tengah: brokers sold fake STRs to nurses who repeatedly failed competency exams at Rp1.5–2.5 million each (Radar Lombok, 2018).

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Situbondo: 23 contractors were reported for using fake SKA/SKT certificates to win APBD tenders worth Rp300 million–Rp2 billion each (LSM Geram Maki report, 2016, re local APBD 2016 projects).

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Banten, August 2025: a man using a forged PERADI ID card was reported to Polda Banten for fraud and embezzlement (Kominfo.co.id, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: No aggregate national figure exists (unverified). Verified case-level costs: Rp538.95 million single-victim loss (Polres Bantul, 2025); tender disqualifications for fake SKK are documented by compliance vendors (CekSKK.com, 2025, anecdotal). Scale of exposure: 1,545,763 health workers nationally (Ke

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Government: KKI "Cek Dokter"/STR verification, free and public, explicitly built for hospital credentialing (KKI); SATUSEHAT SDMK for STR/SIP lifecycle (Kemenkes, 2023); LPJK SIKI database with public SKK lookup; BNSP certificate registry; PISN for underlying diplomas.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Private: cekskk.com and similar aggregators wrapping LPJK data; hospital SIMRS/credentialing modules (Trustmedis and other vendors document STR workflows); background-check firms (Integrity Indonesia) for senior hires.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - No funded Indonesian startup dominates license verification as a product (search, 2026-07).

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: Registries are siloed per profession and per permit layer (STR national, SIP at local government), so a full practitioner check crosses three systems. More fundamentally, the documented frauds are identity-binding failures: Susanto passed because he presented a real doctor's credentials. A registry

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: Each profession already has an accepted single trusted operator (KKI/Kemenkes, LPJK, BNSP, PERADI). Verifiers trust these registries; the failure modes are identity binding and enforcement, which are orthogonal to tamper-evidence. A blockchain of licenses would replicate SATUSEHAT SDMK with extra st

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: KILLED.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem without blockchain? YES.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator? YES — KKI/SATUSEHAT/SIKI are exactly that and are accepted. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: 3. Incumbent ships it in 6 months? YES — Kemenkes and LPJK routinely extend their portals; SIMRS vendors can add credentialing features. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone value? Thin against free state lookups. FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 7 — patient harm and criminal cases yearly; hospitals staff credentialing committees; tender fraud documented.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Market 4 — credentialing/compliance tooling for ~3,000 hospitals and contractors; no verified TAM above $50M (unverified).

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 5 — accreditation-mandated credentialing budgets exist, but the verification itself is free from government.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 3 — accepted single trusted registries per profession.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 5 — UU 17/2023 transition ongoing; lifetime STR reduces recurring verification pressure.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 5 — free government portals plus small aggregators; no dominant private player.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 3 — thin wrapper over state registries, copyable.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: Weighted: 4.7.

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.title: Professional Licensing — License Verification (Health, Construction, Legal)
searchIndex.text: Already killed: free authoritative government lookups; the impostor problem being biometric/identity rather than ledger-shaped; SIP fragmentation solvable only by the state; sub-10% SKK coverage meaning the constrained resource is certification capacity, not verification.
