searchIndex.text: # Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: Researched 2026-07-29. Phase 1 scan, pre-committed rubric.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: Indonesian developers finance construction with buyer money. Pre-project selling works as: developer secures land and building approval (PBG), then markets units under a PPJB (preliminary sale-purchase agreement). PP 12/2021 permits PPJB marketing only after land-status certainty, PBG, utility avail

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: When projects stall, remedies are post-hoc: complaints (now via the government's BENAR-PKP channel), civil suits, or insolvency petitions — and the Supreme Court's position that developer disputes fail the "simple proof" requirement makes PKPU/bankruptcy against developers largely unusable; buyers w

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Buyers/consumers: pay first, carry all completion risk.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Developers (Lippo/Meikarta, Agung Podomoro, mid-tier and small developers): control the funds; resist any lock-up of presale cash.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Banks: disburse KPR indent to developers; also sell voluntary escrow accounts (Kontan explainer) — not mandated for presales.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Notaries/PPAT: paper the PPJB and AJB.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Kementerian PKP: runs BENAR-PKP complaints; drafting a new Housing Law (UU Perumahan) in 2026 to tackle the backlog (ANTARA, 2026).

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - YLKI, courts, and occasionally police (fraud) absorb the disputes.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Meikarta (Lippo, Cikarang): sold aggressively from 2017, stalled; by May 2025 the BENAR-PKP service logged 567 consumer reports. The ministry split refunds into 4 stages: stage 1 = 124 complainants owed Rp30 billion; stage 2 = 274 complainants under validation, Rp73 billion. As of February 2026 on

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Antasari 45 (Jakarta): construction halted since 2014; PKPU filed 2020; rebranded Antasari Place (Properti Indonesia).

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - YLKI 2024: 49 individual housing complaints (4.94% of individual complaints) plus 177 group housing complaints; leading issues: stalled construction (30%), documents/certificates (20%), refunds (16%) (YLKI via Industri Properti/Liputan6, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Buyer trauma is now a demand-side drag: consumers choosing to rent rather than buy presale units (Koran Properti; Kompas, July 2026, "Kenapa konsumen masih terjerat rayuan pengembang nakal?").

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Meikarta alone: Rp103 billion in validated/queued refund claims across stages 1–2 of four stages, from 567 reports (Kementerian PKP, 2025–2026).

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)

searchIndex.text: - Indirect cost: presale distrust suppressing apartment absorption (qualitative; Koran Properti, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Regulation: UU 1/2011 and UU 20/2011 plus PP 12/2021 (PPJB conditions, 20% threshold) — conduct rules, not fund segregation. New Housing Law in drafting (ANTARA, 2026); no mandatory escrow provision verified as of July 2026.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - BENAR-PKP (Kementerian PKP consumer complaint and mediation service, operating since 2025) — post-hoc, non-binding leverage.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Bank escrow accounts: exist as a voluntary commercial product (Kontan); used in some B2B property deals, not standard in consumer presales.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Proptech: Rumah123, Pinhome, Jendela and marketplace/mortgage players do listings and financing referral; hard search found no Indonesian startup operating presale escrow or milestone-release fund custody as of mid-2026.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Regional precedent: Malaysia's Housing Development Account, Singapore project accounts, Dubai RERA escrow — mandated by law in those markets.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: Buyer money still lands on the developer's balance sheet on day one. The 20% rule is under-enforced, disclosure is unaudited, PKPU is blocked, and refunds depend on the developer's goodwill and liquidity — Meikarta's 11% refund completion a year past deadline shows the enforcement void. Nothing in t

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: The fix is fund segregation plus independent milestone verification. Both are delivered by a bank escrow agent operating under regulation — banks are an accepted, trusted, regulated intermediary in Indonesia. A ledger adds nothing a bank trust account plus an audited progress certificate does not; t

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict — KILLED

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 1. Problem survives without blockchain? YES (passes).

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator? YES — a bank-operated escrow with milestone release solves it outright; Malaysia does this with ordinary banking infrastructure. FAILS.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 3. Incumbent ships it in 6 months? Largely — any large bank could productize presale escrow quickly once demand or mandate exists. FAILS.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone value? Only with a mandate: good developers do not need escrow to sell, bad developers will not adopt it voluntarily — adverse selection guts the market absent regulation. FAILS.

searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Severity 8 — documented national scandal (Meikarta), life-savings losses, broken refund process persisting into 2026.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Market 5 — escrow/custody fees on presale volume plausibly $50–250M TAM; (unverified) precisely.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - WTP 3 — beneficiaries (consumers) cannot pay; developers will not pay to constrain their own cash; no compliance mandate exists.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Chain 4 — multi-party, but a regulated bank is an accepted trusted intermediary; anchor case for "database fine."

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 6 — refund failures live through 2026 and a new Housing Law is in drafting, but no escrow mandate is on a clock.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Competition 7 — verified whitespace-adjacent: no operating presale-escrow venture found; only a government complaint channel.

searchIndex.title: Property Pre-Sales & Escrow (Indonesia)
searchIndex.text: - Moat 4 — if escrow were mandated, banks capture it; the workflow is copyable.

searchIndex.text: # Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Problem & Current Workflow

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Indonesian import/export trade and large domestic B2B trade run on documentary credit. For cross-border deals the instrument is the letter of credit (L/C); for domestic trade it is the SKBDN (Surat Kredit Berdokumen Dalam Negeri), the domestic L/C regulated by Bank Indonesia. Workflow: (1) buyer app

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Stakeholders & Who Pays

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Banks' trade finance and KMK units do the work (Mandiri, BRI, BNI, BCA, plus state export financier LPEI/Indonesia Eximbank). Corporate importers/exporters pay fees and interest. Bank Indonesia regulates SKBDN; OJK supervises bank credit; BPK and KPK/Kejaksaan Agung audit and prosecute when state ba

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Trust Breakdown (documented incidents)

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **BNI fictitious L/C, 2003**: Rp 1.7 trillion drained from BNI Kebayoran Baru via fictitious export L/Cs with forged documents and insider cooperation; perpetrator Maria Pauline Lumowa was a fugitive 17 years, extradited from Serbia in 2020 and sentenced to 18 years (JISIP/Mandalanursa journal, 20

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **LPEI export-financing corruption, 2024–2026**: Finance Minister Sri Mulyani reported Rp 2.5 trillion of fraudulent export financing across four companies to the Attorney General in March 2024; the case moved to KPK, which by March 2025 had named 12 suspects including two LPEI managing directors,

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Bank Jakarta (Bank DKI) fictitious invoices, 2026**: BPK findings triggered investigation of Rp 295 billion in working-capital credit to PT Rass Mandiri Utama backed by fictitious invoices and inadequate collateral (Senator.id, July 2026).

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Globally, duplicate financing — pledging the same invoice/cargo to multiple lenders — is trade finance's recognized fraud pattern; GTR documented recycled-invoice and shell-company receivables scams costing individual lenders seven-figure sums, 2022–2024 (GTR Risk, 2024).

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Cost of the Problem

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Rp 1.7 trillion (BNI case, 2003, court records via JISIP 2022).

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Rp 11.7 trillion potential state loss (LPEI case, KPK, 2025).

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Rp 295 billion (Bank Jakarta case, BPK/Senator.id, 2026).

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - ADB put the global trade finance gap at US$2.5 trillion for 2022 (ADB Trade Finance Gaps survey, 2024); fraud risk is one driver of high SME rejection rates (ADB: SME rejection ~41–45%, 2023–2025 surveys).

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Aggregate annual Indonesian trade-finance fraud losses: (unverified) — no named source publishes a total.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07, named)

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **MonetaGo Secure Financing via Swift**: hash-based duplicate-financing registry live on the Swift API channel since 2022, accessible to all 11,000+ Swift member institutions — including Indonesian banks (Swift/MonetaGo, 2022; GTR).

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **ABS Trade Finance Registry, Singapore**: Association of Banks in Singapore selected MonetaGo to run a live national duplicate-financing registry (GTR, 2023).

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Dead consortium chains**: we.trade insolvent 2022, Marco Polo insolvent Feb 2023 (€5.2m debts), Contour shut Nov 2023 processing only 60–70 transactions/month, TradeLens shut 2022 (Ledger Insights, TFG, 2022–2023). Failure cause was economics and adoption, not technology.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Document-checking AI**: Traydstream, Conpend/Surecomp scan L/C documents for discrepancies (global vendors; no verified Indonesian deployments found).

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - **Indonesia**: SLIK (OJK debtor credit registry) is debtor-level, not document-level; INSW handles customs documents, not bank financing. No Indonesian duplicate-financing registry was found in searches as of July 2026.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Why Insufficient

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: Indonesian banks still cannot answer "has this invoice/bill of lading already been financed elsewhere?" SLIK shows a borrower's loans, not the documents behind them. Swift/MonetaGo coverage is opt-in per bank and oriented to cross-border flows; SKBDN and rupiah KMK/invoice financing sit outside any

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Blockchain Test

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: The verification problem is multi-bank, but the parties are all regulated by BI/OJK, which are accepted neutral authorities. Singapore solved the identical problem with a centralized hash registry run by one vendor under the banking association — no chain. Contour/we.trade/Marco Polo demonstrate tha

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Kill Test Verdict

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 1. Without blockchain, problem persists — PASS.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 2. PostgreSQL under a trusted operator (OJK/BI-mandated registry, MonetaGo model) solves it just as well — FAIL.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 3. Six-month ERP feature — pass (it is a cross-bank utility, not a feature), but Swift already distributes MonetaGo to Indonesian banks.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: 4. Standalone value — plausible but consortium sales to state banks are slow.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: **KILLED on question 2.**

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: ## Scores

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Severity 8 — repeated trillion-rupiah frauds (BNI, LPEI) with criminal and regulatory exposure.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Market 5 — registry/verification software TAM in Indonesia plausibly US$50–250M; core losses are large but the sellable product is small.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - WTP 6 — banks budget for fraud controls, but consortium procurement is slow and needs a regulator push.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Chain 4 — multi-org, yet BI/OJK are accepted neutral operators; centralized registry proven equivalent.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Urgency 6 — LPEI prosecution and Bank Jakarta case are live in 2025–2026; no hard regulatory deadline found.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Competition 5 — global registries and doc-check vendors exist and reach Indonesia via Swift; no local incumbent dominant.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: - Moat 6 — a mandated national registry would enjoy network effects, but MonetaGo could win that mandate.

searchIndex.title: Trade Finance & LC Fraud — Indonesia
searchIndex.text: **Weighted: 5.8** — below 7.0 cutoff and killed on the kill test.

searchIndex.text: ## What Would Kill This Idea

searchIndex.text: Exactly what the kill test found: OJK/BI or Himbara banks adopting the Swift/MonetaGo service or commissioning a centralized national registry; MonetaGo signing an ABS-style deal with an Indonesian banking association. Also: SKBDN volumes may be too small to matter (volume data unverified), and the
